data.title: BusyBeaver(6) Is Quite Large
data.author: bdr
data.article_summary: Scott Aaronson讨论了Busy Beaver函数（BB(n)）的最新进展，特别是BB(6)的巨大数值。BB(6)是一个6状态图灵机在 halt 前可以执行的最大步骤数。最新研究显示，BB(6)远大于之前预估的10^36,534，甚至超过10^(10^7)（百万次的十的幂）。团队使用Coq证明了新的下界，并且进一步研究显示BB(6)可能比之前想象的更大，达到2的多次迭代幂次（tetration和pentation）。Aaronson还提到，这些发现可能意味着BB(n)在n为7到9时就可能超出ZFC集合论的独立性，而不是之前认为的n为20或30。此外，Aaronson刚从STOC'2025会议返回，并分享了其关于量子加速的演讲。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Busy Beaver函数（BB）和Graham's Number的比较，及其相关的计算复杂性和实际意义。

不同观点：
• **tromp**：认为尽管BB(6)已经取得了很大进展，但BB(7)是否能超越Graham's Number仍然存疑，并与其他人就此打赌。他引用了相关的数据和资源来支持他的观点，如lambda项数量和6状态图灵机数量的比较。

• **Scarblac**：对BB(748)独立于ZFC（Zermelo-Fraenkel集合论与选择公理）感到惊讶，认为这像是分类错误，表达了对数学独立性结果的困惑。

• **MichaelDickens**：基于新发现，认为BB(7)很可能超过Graham's Number，直觉上觉得从pentation到Graham's Number的技术要求比从47,176,870到`2 <pentate> 5`要简单。

• **phs**：提出一个逻辑学问题，询问用一个五状态图灵机可以枚举的逻辑体系的复杂性。

• **sedatk**：首次接触tetration（迭代指数）的概念，对高阶数学运算的表示方法表示新奇。

• **seeknotfind**：对用10,000,000的10次方颗粒的沙子填满宇宙的类比表示困惑，质疑这种比较的合理性，并提到质量比较更为常见。

• **d_silin**：认为计算复杂性理论的结果揭示了超智能AI的局限性，即使利用全宇宙的资源也无法完成BB(6)的计算，批评了当前对AI能力的夸大。

• **fjfaase**：质疑可见宇宙是否足够大以写下BB(6)的确切值，表现出对Busy Beaver函数巨大数值的惊讶。

• **charcircuit**：回应沙子填满宇宙的类比，认为人们无法直观理解如此大的数字，并建议通过组合和指数增长的方式来表达大数。

• **NooneAtAll3**：建议对Busy Beaver结果感兴趣的人阅读https://www.sligocki.com/，并提到该研究者是Busy Beaver研究的前沿人物，参与了https://bbchallenge.org网站的建设。

补充讨论：
• 对Busy Beaver函数的巨大数值和其在数学及计算复杂性理论中的独立性结果的惊讶和讨论。
• 对如何表达和理解大数的不同观点和类比的讨论。
• 对Busy Beaver函数实际计算能力的质疑和AI能力的反思。

44406171.article_content:
Shtetl-Optimized
The Blog of Scott Aaronson
If you take nothing else from this blog: quantum computers won't
solve hard problems instantly by just trying all solutions in parallel.
Also, please read Zvi Mowshowitz's masterpiece on how to fix K-12 education!
«
Raymond Laflamme (1960-2025)
BusyBeaver(6) is really quite large
For overdetermined reasons, I’ve lately found the world an increasingly terrifying and depressing place.  It’s gotten harder and harder to concentrate on research, or even popular science writing.  Every so often, though, something breaks through that wakes my inner child, reminds me of why I fell in love with research thirty years ago, and helps me forget about the triumphantly strutting factions working to destroy everything I value.
Back in 2022, I
reported an exciting advance
in
BusyBeaverology
: namely, whereas we previously knew merely that BB(6) > 10
36,534
, Pavel Kropitz managed to show that
BB(6) >
15
10.
For those tuning in from home, here BB(6) is the 6
th
Busy Beaver number, i.e. the maximum number of steps that a 6-state Turing machine with a {0,1} alphanet can take before halting, when run on an initially all-0 input tape. Also, the left-superscript means
tetration
, or iterated exponentiation: for example,
15
10 means 10 to the 10 to the 10 and so on 15 times.
By comparison, last year the international “BBchallenge” team
determined that BB(5) is “merely” 47,176,870
(see also
Quanta
magazine’s
superb feature article
on that milestone).  So, between 5 and 6 is where the Busy Beaver function makes its leap, from the millions to beyond the bounds of observable reality.
But if you thought that was the end of the BB(6) story, think again!  Eleven days ago, Tristan Sterin, who organized the BBchallenge the team, emailed to tell me that a team member with the handle “mxdys”
improved the BB(6) bound yet further
, to
BB(6) >
10,000,000
10
(i.e., 10 to the 10 to the 10 and so on 10 million times), with a
correctness proof in Coq
.  Then, three days ago, Tristan wrote
again
to say that mxdys has
improved the bound
again
, to
$$ BB(6) \gt ^{^{{^9}2}2}2 $$
I.e., BB(6) is at least 2 tetrated to the 2 tetrated to the 2 tetrated to the 9.  So in particular, BB(6) is at least 2 pentated to the 5, where
pentation
is iterated tetration, i.e. the operation that is to tetration as tetration is to exponentiation, expenentiation is to multiplication, and multiplication is to addition.
Last week, when we “merely” knew that BB(6) >
10,000,000
10, I talked to a journalist who asked me to give an intuitive sense of how big such a number is.  So I said, imagine you had
10,000,000
10 grains of sand. Then you could … well, uh … you could fill about
10,000,000
10 copies of the observable universe with that sand.  I hope that helps people visualize it!
The journalist also asked: have these new discoveries about BB(6) caused me to rethink any broader beliefs about the Busy Beaver function? And I mean, yes and no: it was
always
completely within the realm of possibility that BB(6) would already be, not some puny little thing like 10
36,534
, but way out in iteration land. Now that we know for sure that it is, though, maybe I ought to conjecture that the value of BB(n) becomes independent of the ZFC axioms of set theory already when n is 7 or 8 or 9, rather than when it’s 20 or 30 or whatever. (Currently, we
know
that
BB(n) becomes independent of ZFC only when n=643.)
Unrelated Update:
I’m just now returning to the US from
STOC’2025
in Prague, where I saw lots of old friends and learned many interesting new things, again helping to distract me from the state of the world!    Many I’ll write about some of those things in a future post.  For now, though, anyone who’s interested in my STOC plenary lecture, entitled “The Status of Quantum Speedups,” can
check out the PowerPoint slides here
.

data.title: Addictions Are Being Engineered
data.author: echollama
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体的道德问题、增长与投资的关系、技术与社会连接的本质

不同观点：
• klik99认为，外部投资是公司失去道德的主要原因，公司为了达到增长和季度目标，往往会忽视道德问题，专注于用户活跃度。投资者的法律义务使公司难以自主决策，最终导致成瘾性设计成为指南。
• spenjuly推荐《Addiction by Design》一书，指出赌博行业的成瘾设计与当今智能手机/互联网行业的相似性，暗示当前问题有历史根源。
• smikhanov质疑klik99的观点，认为不需要抱怨道德问题，可以通过低成本的方式（如外包和自助开发）运行社交网络，不必依赖风险投资。
• fullshark暗示政府监管可能是解决问题的办法，但未详细阐述。
• scoofy分享了自己在没有资金支持下建立维基的经历，强调了资金对于推动产品广泛使用的重要性，但也表示愿意以慢而稳的方式发展。
• divbzero指出原文未提到Facebook在2011年通过News Feed普及了参与算法，提醒读者注意历史背景。
• johncole提出一个思想实验，如果这些应用程序由非营利组织拥有，是否还会成瘾，认为VC资金只是加速了最终状态的到来。
• closetkantian分享了自己使用电子墨水屏手机的经验，指出这种设备减少了社交媒体的吸引力，同时提高了阅读书籍的效率。
• alwa认为技术产品不一定要增长，可以选择保持小规模和人性化，指出当前仍有机会制作小而美的产品，不必追求大规模资本。
• scottgg认同当前问题的显而易见性，但指出草根项目难以与大量资金竞争。
• quaintdev认为应停止建立社交网络，鼓励面对面的社交互动，强调非语言交流在建立信任中的重要性。
• liendolucas质疑是否有可能通过收费的方式创建一个完全无害的社交网络，并询问其成功可能性。
• ruined指出原文未提及联合平台，认为这是一个重大遗漏。

补充讨论：
• 不同评论者对社交媒体的成瘾性设计及其与投资的关系有不同看法，部分人认为投资加速了成瘾性设计，而另一些人则认为成瘾性设计不可避免。
• 部分评论者提出替代方案，如政府监管、非营利组织拥有、低成本自助开发和面对面社交互动等。
• 技术产品的增长是否必要以及如何在小规模和人性化之间取得平衡也是一个重要的讨论点。

• klik99认为，外部投资是公司失去道德的主要原因，公司为了达到增长和季度目标，往往会忽视道德问题，专注于用户活跃度。投资者的法律义务使公司难以自主决策，最终导致成瘾性设计成为指南。
• spenjuly推荐《Addiction by Design》一书，指出赌博行业的成瘾设计与当今智能手机/互联网行业的相似性，暗示当前问题有历史根源。
• smikhanov质疑klik99的观点，认为不需要抱怨道德问题，可以通过低成本的方式（如外包和自助开发）运行社交网络，不必依赖风险投资。
• fullshark暗示政府监管可能是解决问题的办法，但未详细阐述。
• scoofy分享了自己在没有资金支持下建立维基的经历，强调了资金对于推动产品广泛使用的重要性，但也表示愿意以慢而稳的方式发展。
• divbzero指出原文未提到Facebook在2011年通过News Feed普及了参与算法，提醒读者注意历史背景。
• johncole提出一个思想实验，如果这些应用程序由非营利组织拥有，是否还会成瘾，认为VC资金只是加速了最终状态的到来。
• closetkantian分享了自己使用电子墨水屏手机的经验，指出这种设备减少了社交媒体的吸引力，同时提高了阅读书籍的效率。
• alwa认为技术产品不一定要增长，可以选择保持小规模和人性化，指出当前仍有机会制作小而美的产品，不必追求大规模资本。
• scottgg认同当前问题的显而易见性，但指出草根项目难以与大量资金竞争。
• quaintdev认为应停止建立社交网络，鼓励面对面的社交互动，强调非语言交流在建立信任中的重要性。
• liendolucas质疑是否有可能通过收费的方式创建一个完全无害的社交网络，并询问其成功可能性。
• ruined指出原文未提及联合平台，认为这是一个重大遗漏。

补充讨论：
• 不同评论者对社交媒体的成瘾性设计及其与投资的关系有不同看法，部分人认为投资加速了成瘾性设计，而另一些人则认为成瘾性设计不可避免。
• 部分评论者提出替代方案，如政府监管、非营利组织拥有、低成本自助开发和面对面社交互动等。
• 技术产品的增长是否必要以及如何在小规模和人性化之间取得平衡也是一个重要的讨论点。

data.title: Sirius: A GPU-native SQL engine
data.author: qianli_cs
data.article_summary: Sirius 是一个 GPU 原生的 SQL 引擎，通过 Substrait 查询格式与现有数据库（如 DuckDB）集成，无需重写查询或进行重大系统更改。它适用于交互式分析、金融工作负载和 ETL 任务，在 TPC-H 测试中，SF=100 时相较于 CPU 查询引擎有约 10 倍的速度提升。Sirius 支持 Ubuntu 20.04 及以上版本、NVIDIA Volta 或更高版本的 GPU、CUDA 11.2 及以上，以及 CMake 3.30.4 及以上版本。用户可以通过 AWS 镜像、Docker 镜像或手动安装来配置环境。构建 Sirius 需要克隆其仓库并使用特定命令进行编译，如需使用 Python API，还需额外安装相关包。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Substrait的应用及其在不同引擎和硬件加速上的可行性和挑战

不同观点：
• cpard：对Substrait被更多地使用表示欢迎，提到它已被DuckDB等引擎支持，并指出Apache Gluten项目使用Substrait将Velox作为Spark的执行引擎。认为尽管Substrait有局限性，但需要更多这样的项目来推动其发展。

• b0a04gl：指出查询计划与其生成引擎紧密相关，包括成本模型、内存布局、并行策略和代码生成行为等。虽然Substrait实现了结构的可移植性，但实际执行效率依赖于引擎特定的重写。例如，在DuckDB中优化的计划在Sirius中可能表现不佳，除非进行重塑。

• tucnak：通过PG-Strom项目类比，讨论了GPU在数据库应用中的适应性问题。提到NVIDIA的GPUDirect技术和AMD的Alveo系列加速器。认为GPU的AI计算能力虽然常被强调，但其在计算网络中的应用（如数据移动和中间计算）可能更有前景。同时，提到Postgres的扩展性和外国数据API，指出一些替代SQL引擎可能在朝错误方向发展。

补充讨论：
• tucnak引用了多个技术项目和文献（如PG-Strom、Versal、Corundum），进一步探讨了GPU和加速器在数据库和网络计算中的应用实例和潜力。
• 争议焦点之一是GPU是否适合数据库操作，尤其是在与传统SQL引擎比较时，GPU的角色和效率问题。
• 另一个讨论点是Substrait在不同引擎间的执行效率问题，以及如何在不同引擎之间实现查询计划的优化和重写。

Sirius is a GPU-native SQL engine. It plugs into existing databases such as DuckDB via the standard Substrait query format, requiring no query rewrites or major system changes. Sirius currently supports DuckDB and Doris (coming soon), other systems marked with * are on our roadmap.
Performance
Running TPC-H on SF=100, Sirius achieves ~10x speedup over existing CPU query engines at the same hardware rental cost, making it well-suited for interactive analytics, financial workloads, and ETL jobs.
Supported OS/GPU/CUDA/CMake
Ubuntu >= 20.04
NVIDIA Volta™ or higher with compute capability 7.0+
CUDA >= 11.2
CMake >= 3.30.4 (follow this
instruction
to upgrade CMake)
We recommend building Sirius with at least
16 vCPUs
to ensure faster compilation.
Dependencies (Option 1): Use AWS Image
For users who have access to AWS and want to launch AWS EC2 instances to run Sirius, the following images are prepared with dependencies fully installed.
AMI Name
AWS Region
AMI ID
Sirius Dependencies AMI (Ubuntu 24.04) 20250611
us-east-1
ami-06020f2b2161f5d62
us-east-2
ami-016b589f441fecc5d
us-west-2
ami-060043bae3f9b5eb4
Supported EC2 instances: G4dn, G5, G6, Gr6, G6e, P4, P5, P6.
Dependencies (Option 2): Use Docker Image
To use the docker image with dependencies fully installed:
sudo docker run --gpus all -it yifeiyang7/sirius_dependencies:latest bash
If encounting errors like the following when running the docker image as above:
docker: Error response from daemon: could not select device driver “” with capabilities: [[gpu]].
This means
nvidia-driver
or
nvidia-container-toolkit
is not installed.
To install
nvidia-driver
:
sudo apt install nvidia-driver-535
To install
nvidia-container-toolkit
, please follow the
instructions
.
Finally restart docker by
sudo systemctl restart docker
Dependencies (Option 3): Install Manually
Install duckdb dependencies
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y git g++ cmake ninja-build libssl-dev
Install CUDA
If CUDA is not installed, download
here
. Follow the instructions for the deb(local) installer and complete the
post-installation steps
.
Verify installation:
nvcc --version
nvidia-smi
Install libcudf dependencies
libcudf will be installed via conda/miniconda. Miniconda can be downloaded
here
. After downloading miniconda, install libcudf by running these commands:
conda create --name libcudf-env
conda activate libcudf-env
conda install -c rapidsai -c conda-forge -c nvidia rapidsai::libcudf
Set the environment variables
LIBCUDF_ENV_PREFIX
to the conda environment's path. For example, if we installed miniconda in
~/miniconda3
and installed libcudf in the conda environment
libcudf-env
, then we would set the
LIBCUDF_ENV_PREFIX
to
~/miniconda3/envs/libcudf-env
.
export LIBCUDF_ENV_PREFIX={PATH to libcudf-env}
It is recommended to add the environment variables to your
bashrc
to avoid repetition.
Building Sirius
To clone the Sirius repository:
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/sirius-db/sirius.git
cd sirius
export SIRIUS_HOME_PATH=`pwd`
cd duckdb
mkdir -p extension_external && cd extension_external
git clone https://github.com/duckdb/substrait.git
cd substrait
git reset --hard ec9f8725df7aa22bae7217ece2f221ac37563da4 #go to the right commit hash for duckdb substrait extension
cd $SIRIUS_HOME_PATH
The
--recurse-submodules
will ensure DuckDB is pulled which is required to build the extension.
To build Sirius:
make -j {nproc}
Optionally, to use the Python API in Sirius, we also need to build the duckdb-python package with the following commands:
cd duckdb/tools/pythonpkg/
pip install .
cd $SIRIUS_HOME_PATH

pip install .

data.title: Parsing JSON in Forty Lines of Awk
data.author: thefilmore
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种在POSIX shell中使用`awk`解析JSON的方法。JSON因其层次结构和字符问题，在Unix shell中不易处理。常见工具如`jq`可以正确解析JSON，但需要额外安装。作者选择使用Python或在现有shell脚本中实现JSON解析器。文章详细描述了用`awk`编写一个简化JSON解析函数的过程，该函数通过递归解析JSON文档并根据点号路径提取键值。函数处理对象和数组，通过循环字符实现解析，但有一些局限性，如仅支持有效JSON输入。示例代码展示了如何调用该函数提取和处理JSON数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Awk及Unix shell工具在处理JSON等复杂数据格式时的局限性，以及可能的替代方案。

不同观点：
• [chaps] 认为Awk虽然强大，但在某些功能上存在缺陷，比如处理中间列或复杂数据格式时，命令会变得冗长，违背了Unix快速实验的精神。同时指出jq和SQL也存在类似问题。
• [chubot] 支持[chaps]对Awk的批评，并进一步指出Unix shell在处理JSON等层次化数据格式时的不足。提出自己开发的OSH和YSH（Oil Shell）作为解决方案，这些工具内置对JSON的支持，并具备处理递归数据结构的能力。通过示例代码展示了如何使用OSH和YSH处理JSON数据，并提到OSH在性能上已经优于Bash。
• [teddyh] 简短指出Unicode转义序列的问题，虽然没有展开，但暗示了在处理文本编码时可能遇到的复杂性。
• [wutwutwat] 提出一种哲学性的反对意见，认为技术人员往往只关注技术上的可行性，而忽视了是否应当这样做，暗示在某些情况下使用不适合的工具处理复杂数据可能并不明智。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Awk及传统Unix shell工具在处理现代数据格式（如JSON）时的能力不足。
• [chubot]通过推广自己开发的OSH和YSH，提出了一个技术上的替代路径，并通过具体示例和性能比较来证明其优越性。
• [wutwutwat]的评论引发对技术选择合理性的深层次思考，提醒人们关注工具使用的适当性。

总结：讨论主要围绕Awk及Unix shell在处理复杂数据格式时的局限性展开，同时提出了现代化的替代方案（如OSH和YSH），并涉及技术选择的哲学性反思。

JSON is not a friendly format to the Unix shell — it’s hierarchical, and
cannot be reasonably split on any character (other than the newline, which is
not very useful) as that character might be included in a string. There are
well-known tools such as
jq
that let you correctly parse
JSON documents in the shell, but all require an additional dependency. Another
option is to use Python, which is ubiquitous enough that it can be expected to
be installed on virtually every machine, and for new projects would be the
recommended option.
However, I already had a working POSIX shell script that now had a requirement
to read and parse JSON. It had previously extracted values from HTML which,
while also being hierarchical, can be reliably split on certain characters (the
angle brackets) for basic extraction of values. awk is the closest thing to a
real programming language that’s available in the POSIX shell, so I thought I’d
try to write a basic JSON parser in it. I had already written a full-blown
one
before, so I knew it was doable, but

notoriously
tricky
to get completely right,
despite its simple grammar. The following code assumes that it will be fed
valid JSON. It has some basic validation as a function of the parsing and will
most likely throw an error if it encounters something strange, but there are no
guarantees beyond that. In my case, I’m reading JSON from a single, trusted
source, so this is an acceptable constraint.

data.title: Is being bilingual good for your brain?
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了双语能力是否对大脑有益。多项研究表明，掌握多种语言可能提高执行功能，如抗干扰能力、任务规划能力和更新信念的能力，甚至可能使痴呆症发病时间推迟约四年。然而，一些研究结果无法重复，令专家质疑这些认知优势是否真实存在以及具体表现如何。总体而言，学习语言的实际益处更为明确，但其对大脑的长期影响仍需进一步研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多语言能力的益处与挑战，以及多语言对大脑和文化的影响

不同观点：
• afiodorov认为，多语言使用能保持大脑活跃，但也指出即使多年使用非母语语言，仍可能面临流利度不足的挑战。他强调了文化沉浸对语言掌握的重要性，并提到使用母语时的舒适感。
• heresie-daccord强调，多语言能力能促进社会互动和文化理解，是解决问题的重要工具。他认为学习多种语言可以培养认知适应能力，但这种能力未必能普遍适用。
• FlyingSnake赞美多语言生活带来的文化体验，认为人类天生适合多语言，并通过个人丰富的语言使用经验展示了多语言的美妙之处。
• hombre_fatal引用了研究，指出语言对大脑的影响在儿童和老年人中更为显著，而年轻成年人的优势可能不明显。
• dehrmann质疑在有限时间内，多语言使用是否是最佳的大脑刺激方式，提出了其他活动如演奏乐器或体育锻炼的比较。
• keiferski指出，多语言不仅意味着语言技能，还包括对多种文化的深入理解，这能提升一个人的视角和理解能力。
• nayuki认为，多语言可以帮助区分同音词，提高语言精确性，例如在英语中通过对比其他语言的词汇来区分同音词。
• dumroll基于自身经验，认为在美国等多语言可能带来更多挑战而非优势，特别是在职业和社交机会方面，并强调文化沉浸的重要性。
• xvilka提到Language Transfer项目，作为一个学习多语言的资源。
• agumonkey分享了学习拉丁语带来的认知重构体验，认为这能帮助连接新想法。
• zeroCalories持反对观点，认为除非对某种文化有浓厚兴趣，否则学习英语以外的语言没有必要，尤其在未来AI翻译技术发展的情况下。
• AdrianB1对科技行业中双语人士是否比单语人士更具优势持怀疑态度，认为这仅是 speculation。

补充讨论：
• 多语言对大脑的影响在不同年龄段的效果差异是一个讨论焦点，特别是儿童和老年人的优势更显著。
• 多语言带来的文化理解被认为是重要的附加价值，而不仅仅是语言技能的掌握。
• 多语言在实际生活中的应用和文化沉浸被多次强调，尤其是对长期居住和职业发展的影响。
• 有争议的观点主要集中在多语言在现代社会（如美国）中的实际优势，以及在AI技术发展背景下学习多语言的必要性。

44406140.article_content:
Science & technology
|
Well informed
Is being bilingual good for your brain?
Perhaps. Learning languages offers other, more concrete benefits
Share
Illustration: Cristina Spanò
Jun 27th 2025
|
3 min read
R
eams of papers
have been published on the cognitive advantages of multilingualism. Beyond the conversational doors it can open, multilingualism is supposed to improve “executive function”, a loose concept that includes the ability to ignore distractions, plan complex tasks and update beliefs as new information arrives. Most striking, numerous studies have even shown that bilinguals undergo a later onset of dementia, perhaps of around four years, on average. But some of these studies have failed to replicate, leaving experts wondering whether the effect is real, and if so, what exactly it consists of.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（特别是大型语言模型，LLM）对社会、法律和就业市场的潜在影响，以及对此的不同观点。

不同观点：
• chisleu认为LLM技术将对世界产生巨大影响，尤其是在中美AI竞争的背景下。他强调LLM已经在实际工作中展现出巨大潜力，比如自动化任务、提高工作效率，甚至开始替代部分初级工程师的工作。他建议人们积极学习如何整合和利用LLM技术，以应对即将到来的技术变革和社会影响。他特别指出，技术进步将对社会底层人群影响最大，可能导致更严重的贫富差距。

• leptons对某些政治立场（如"州权"问题）在讨论中的不一致性提出质疑。虽然没有详细展开，但他的评论暗示了对某些政治言论在技术议题上自相矛盾的不满。

• techpineapple指出美国共和党内部在技术进步问题上的分歧，尤其是自由意志主义者希望自动化所有工作岗位，而传统保守派如Tucker Carlson则担心自动化（如完全自动驾驶技术）会导致大量失业，从而反对这种技术进步。这反映了在同一政党内对技术发展的不同态度。

补充讨论：
• chisleu详细描述了LLM在实际工作中的应用场景，比如更新JIRA票据、从wiki中提取内容、连接数据库等，展示了LLM如何通过提高效率来替代部分工作岗位。
• techpineapple提到的关于政治派别对自动化的矛盾态度，揭示了技术进步带来的就业问题已经成为政治讨论中的一个重要议题。
• 整个讨论还暗示了对未来技术发展不可预测性的担忧，尤其是LLM对就业市场和社会结构的深远影响。chisleu特别提到，技术进步可能导致一个“赛博朋克”式的未来，贫富差距加大，社会底层人群的生活更加艰难。

data.title: Show HN: I'm an airline pilot – I built interactive graphs/globes of my flights
data.author: jamesharding
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一位英航空客A350副驾驶的飞行经历分享。自2023年以来，他一直在伦敦希思罗机场驾驶A350，之前从2016年起驾驶A320系列。他通过英航学员计划加入公司，完成了在西班牙FTEJerez的ATPL课程。他的飞行生涯始于加拿大，获得滑翔机驾照和私人飞行驾照。他使用LogTen Pro记录航班，并通过SQL查询和3D可视化展示飞行日志。文章还介绍了不同年份的飞行小时数、航班距离与时间的关系以及英航的标准操作程序，如监控进场和正副驾驶职责分配等。通过可视化工具，他展示了飞行的国家和机场分布以及年度飞行时数。
data.comments_summary:

• **对统计数据和可视化改进的建议**：
  - [weinzierl] 建议将飞行辐射暴露数据整合到仪表板中，以增加实用性。

• **对项目潜力和职业影响的看法**：
  - [the_arun] 表达了对多领域专家的钦佩，并希望自己也能在主业之外有所作为。

  - [amelius] 建议可以将该项目产品化，让飞行员可以在LinkedIn等平台上展示，以增强职业形象。

补充讨论：
• **工具和技术的推荐**：
  - [jakub_g] 推荐了GCMap工具，可以根据IATA机场代码绘制航线，并分享了使用URL参数的技巧。

• **对具体可视化效果的评价**：
  - [jorisboris] 对目的地矩阵表示新奇，之前从未见过类似的可视化。
  - [18172828286177] 对项目整体表示赞赏，认为作为飞行员能完成如此精致的软件项目非常 impressive。

争议焦点：
• **飞行员职业中的沟通摩擦和幸存者偏差问题**：
  - [ok_computer] 提出的关于飞行员与副驾驶沟通摩擦以及职业中是否存在幸存者偏差或不愿寻求帮助的问题，引发对该职业潜在问题的思考。

Statistics

LogTen Pro

to

Check out my 3D globes page
Annual Hours
How many hours have I been strapped into an aircraft each year? In aviation, we log time from "brakes off" to "brakes on". Some acronym definitions:
P1/PIC
: Pilot in Command
P1US/PICUS
: Pilot in Command, Under Supervision
P2
: Pilot 2
Heavy
: "Extra" pilot on long trips. On jump seat for take off and landing.
At British Airways, the P1 and P2 sectors are usually shared between Captains and FOs, and whoever is P1 "runs" the sector. The Captain is always in command throughout the sector, but FOs are empowered to make decisions and run sectors as
PIC under supervision
.
BA SOPs also dictate that every approach is flown as a
monitored approach
. At top of descent, the P2 will become Pilot Flying, and will fly the approach to 1000ft AGL, where P1 will retake control to land.
Cumulative Hours
The time per-aircraft is separated by
ICAO Type Designator
codes. The A320 family includes "CEO" (A320) and "NEO" (A32N) variants, in addition to A319 and A321 variants.
Flight Time vs Distance
One would expect flight time to increase linearly with distance, which is approximately true. However, due to prevailing winds, often the outbound and inbound flights from London have different times.
The distance measurement in this graph is the
great circle distance
between airports. You can graphically see that Westbound flights from London take longer outbound due to headwinds.

data.title: Boeing uses potatoes to test wi-fi (2012)
data.author: m-hodges
data.article_summary: Boeing使用土豆代替乘客测试机舱内的Wi-Fi信号。由于土豆与电子信号的互动方式类似于人体，且不会像人一样感到无聊，研究人员在退役飞机的座位上放置了大量土豆进行信号测试。测试确保乘客在机舱内不同座位上都能获得稳定的Wi-Fi信号，同时符合安全标准。土豆的总重量达到20,000磅（9,000公斤）。此外，土豆还有许多其他用途，如制造纸张、衣物、葡萄糖以及用于美容和发电等，欧洲土豆贸易协会期待未来进行更多类似实验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：飞机上的电源、WiFi可靠性以及相关技术挑战

不同观点：
• deathanatos：基于个人经历，对飞机上的电源和WiFi的可靠性提出质疑。他描述了多次在飞机上遇到电源插座故障的问题，比如插座损坏或无法供电，并用技术术语"crashloop"形容插座反复失灵的现象。他还指出，虽然信号强度可能很好，但乘客实际体验到的问题往往与理论不符。

• arghwhat：讨论了在飞机客舱中提供WiFi的技术挑战，尤其是处理大量设备同时通信的问题。他指出，过去由于技术限制，一个慢速设备就可能使整个WiFi系统失效。不过，他也提到WiFi 7的新技术特性（如抗拥塞和频道优化）可能改善这种情况。

44406549.article_content:
Image caption,
Potatoes' 'interactions' with electronic signals mimic those of a human body, according to Boeing
US planemaker Boeing used an unusual substitute for passengers to test its in-flight wi-fi  system - potatoes.
Passenger seats on a decommissioned plane were loaded with huge sacks of the tubers for several days as signal strengths were checked.
The company's researchers say that potatoes "interact" with electronic signals in a similar way to humans.
The technique also took advantage of the fact that spuds - unlike humans - never get bored.
Boeing's engineers did a number of tests to ensure that passengers would get the strongest possible wi-fi signal while in the air, all while meeting safety standards that protect against interference with an aircraft's electrical systems.
Wireless signals fluctuate randomly in the enclosed space of an aeroplane cabin as people move about.
This means that signal distribution is uneven throughout the cabin, with weaker and stronger connectivity in different seats.
"You want your laptop to work anywhere it's located on your seat, [but] there can be significant signal changes just due to the location of the laptop," said Boeing engineer Dennis Lewis.
To test the signal distribution, the firm turned to spuds instead of human test subjects, filling the seats with 20,000lbs (9,000kg) of potatoes in sacks.
According to Boeing, potatoes' "interactions" with electronic signals mimic those of a human body, making them "the perfect stand-in for people who would otherwise have had to sit motionless for days while the data was gathered".
Image caption,
Boeing filled the seats with 20,000lbs (9,000kg) of potatoes in sacks
The UK Potato Council said many people underestimated the humble potato's alternative uses.
"[The examples are] in paper and ink manufacturing, potato starch is used in clothing to strengthen the fibres so they don't break during weaving, and for sweetening - glucose can be extracted from potato starch," said the council's spokeswoman.
"For beauty and sores - potatoes have calming, decongestant and astringent properties and raw potatoes can calm tired eyes, potato as alcohol, and potatoes can produce electricity."
Frederic Rosseneu of the European Potato Trade Association Europatat said the organisation was "looking forward to other experiments in which spuds can help to make our lives more convenient".

data.title: ZeQLplus: Terminal SQLite Database Browser
data.author: amadeuspagel
data.article_summary: ZeQL+ 是一个开源的终端 SQLite 数据库浏览器，具有快速、轻量、无依赖等特点。它可以在 macOS、Linux 和 Windows 10+ 系统上运行，支持打开任意 SQLite 数据库文件、浏览表和分页查看表行，还能运行自定义 SQL 查询并查看结果。用户可以从发布页面下载预构建的二进制文件，直接运行而无需安装。此外，ZeQL+ 使用 Vlang 开发，用户也可以从源码构建。项目遵循 MIT 许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[SQL工具的比较与使用体验]

不同观点：
• **amadeuspagel 的观点**：该工具是其使用过的同类工具中最好的，尤其是能够流式传输查询结果（无需LIMIT即可查看SELECT查询的初步结果）并以表格形式展示。不过，他提到工具经常崩溃，这是其主要缺点。

• **smartmic 的观点**：对该工具使用V语言编写感到有趣，并表示会因为这一点而去尝试使用该工具。这表明他对工具使用的编程语言有特别的兴趣，并持开放态度。

• **CraigJPerry 的观点**：认为该工具的用户界面与Harlequin工具非常相似，并提供了一个GitHub链接。他的评论暗示可能存在设计或功能上的借鉴，或者至少是值得比较的工具。

• **nodesocket 的观点**：他更关注一个简洁、无膨胀的SQLite资源管理器，并且已经部署了sqlite-web工具。他对sqlite-web的无外部依赖和只读模式下的表现感到满意，但也提到如果使用CLI工具，仍需通过SSH访问远程服务器上的数据库文件，这可能带来不便。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：工具的稳定性是amadeuspagel提出的主要问题，他赞赏功能的同时也对其经常崩溃表示不满。
• **工具选择**：nodesocket通过实际使用经验推荐了sqlite-web，强调了其在容器化部署和无外部依赖方面的优势。
• **编程语言兴趣**：smartmic对工具的技术栈（使用V语言）表示了特别的兴趣，这显示了部分用户可能对新技术或特定编程语言有偏好，并因此影响其工具选择。

这些观点展示了用户在选择SQL工具时对功能、稳定性、用户界面设计以及技术实现的不同关注点。

data.author: rntn

It’s a tumultuous time for copyright in the United States, with dozens of potentially
economy-shaking
AI copyright lawsuits
winding
through the courts
. It’s also the most turbulent moment in the US Copyright Office’s history. Described as “
sleepy
” in the past, the Copyright Office has taken on new prominence during the AI boom, issuing
key rulings
about
AI and copyright
. It also hasn’t had a leader in more than a month.
In May, Copyright Register Shira Perlmutter was abruptly fired by email by the White House’s deputy director of personnel. Perlmutter is now
suing
the Trump administration, alleging that her firing was invalid; the government
maintains
that the executive branch has the authority to dismiss her. Despite the firing, Perlmutter still characterizes herself as the Copyright Register. “Despite Mr. Perkins’s claim that he is Acting Register of Copyrights, I remain Register of Copyrights and therefore am required by law to fulfill my above-described statutory obligations,” she said in a declaration in May. But much of her lawsuit centers on how she's been rendered unable to effectively perform the duties of the office.
As the legality of the ouster is debated, the reality within the office is this: There’s effectively nobody in charge. And without a leader actually showing up at work, the Copyright Office is not totally business-as-usual; in fact, there’s debate over whether the copyright certificates it’s issuing could be challenged.
The firing followed a pattern. The USCO is part of the Library of Congress; Perlmutter had been appointed to her role by Librarian of Congress Carla Hayden. A few days before Perlmutter’s dismissal, Hayden, who had been in her role since 2016, was also
fired by the White House via email
. The White House
appointed
Deputy Attorney General
Todd Blanche
, who had previously served as President Trump’s defense attorney, as the new acting Librarian of Congress.
Two days after Pelmutter’s firing, Justice Department official Paul Perkins
showed up at the Copyright Office
, along with his colleague Brian Nieves. According to an affidavit from Perlmutter, they were carrying “printed versions of emails” from Blanche indicating that they had been appointed to new roles within the Copyright Office. Perkins, the email said, was designated as Acting Register of Copyrights. In other words, he was Perlmutter’s replacement.
But was Blanche actually the acting Librarian, and thus able to appoint Perkins as such? Within the Library of Congress, someone else had already assumed the role—Robert Newlen, Hayden’s former second-in-command, who has
worked at the LOC
since the 1970s. Following Hayden’s ouster, Newlen emailed LOC staff asserting that
he
was the acting Librarian—never mentioning Blanche—and noting that “Congress is engaged with the White House” on how to proceed.
In her lawsuit, Perlmutter argues that only the Librarian of Congress can fire and appoint a new Register. In a filing on Tuesday, defendants argued that the president does indeed have the authority to fire and appoint the Librarian of Congress and that his appointees then have the ability to choose a new Copyright Register.
Neither the Department of Justice nor the White House responded to requests for comment on this issue; the Library of Congress declined to comment.
Perkins and Nieves did not enter the USCO office or assume the roles they purported to fill the day they showed up. And since they left, sources within the Library of Congress tell WIRED, they have never returned, nor have they assumed any of the duties associated with the roles. These sources say that Congress is in talks with the White House to reach an agreement over these personnel disputes.
A congressional aide familiar with the situation told WIRED that Blanche, Perkins, and Nieves had not shown up for work “because they don’t have jobs to show up to.” The aide continued: “As we’ve always maintained, the President has no authority to appoint them. Robert Newlen has always been the Acting Librarian of Congress.”
If talks are happening, they remain out of public view. But Perlmutter does have some members of Congress openly on her side. “The president has no authority to remove the Register of Copyrights. That power lies solely with the Librarian of Congress. I’m relieved that the situation at the Library and Copyright Office has stabilized following the administration’s unconstitutional attempt to seize control for the executive branch. I look forward to quickly resolving this matter in a bipartisan way,” Senator Alex Padilla tells WIRED in a statement.
In the meantime, the Copyright Office is in the odd position of attempting to carry on as though it wasn’t missing its head. Immediately after Perlmutter’s dismissal, the Copyright Office paused issuing registration certificates “out of an abundance of caution,” according to USCO spokesperson Lisa Berardi Marflak, who says the pause impacted around 20,000

主要讨论点：HPE收购Juniper的战略及其影响

不同观点：
• **estebarb的观点**：对HPE收购Juniper表示不理解。他们认为HPE已经有Aruba（在有线交换机领域很强）和Cray（拥有先进的网络技术），因此不需要再收购Juniper。他们质疑HPE是否真的缺乏内部人才。

• **bc569a80a344f9c的观点**：对HPE收购Juniper表示兴趣，并提到此次收购需要HPE退出SMB品牌Instant On。他们关注此举对企业客户竞争格局的影响，并指出数据中心用例的潜力。他们特别提到Mist的AI/ML功能如何改进运营，特别是在自动化硬件故障处理方面的优势。

补充讨论：
• **竞争格局的变化**：bc569a80a344f9c提到，退出Instant On品牌可能影响企业客户的选择，因为这些客户通常更倾向于选择Aruba的传统产品。

• **技术优势**：bc569a80a344f9c强调Mist的AI/ML功能在自动化和故障检测方面的独特性，认为这是竞争对手难以复制的优势。

争议焦点：
• **收购Juniper的必要性**：estebarb质疑HPE在已经有强大内部资源的情况下，是否有必要收购Juniper，而bc569a80a344f9c则关注收购带来的潜在技术和市场影响。

• **对竞争格局的影响**：bc569a80a344f9c担心退出Instant On品牌可能削弱企业在SMB市场的竞争力，而estebarb没有提到这一点。

总体来看，评论者对HPE收购Juniper的战略持有不同看法，主要围绕收购的必要性和对市场竞争的影响展开讨论。

data.title: Lima Site 85: How a CIA Helicopter Defended a Secret U.S. Radar Facility
data.author: davikr
data.article_summary: during the Vietnam War, a CIA-operated Bell 205 helicopter made history by shooting down a modified North Vietnamese An-2 bomber near Lima Site 85, a secret U.S. radar facility in Laos. Lima Site 85, located atop Phou Pha Thi mountain, played a crucial role in guiding U.S. bombing missions over North Vietnam using the AN/TSQ-81 radar system. On a morning in 1968, a North Vietnamese An-2 plane approached the site to disrupt its operations. Due to the covert nature of the site, its defense fell to the CIA-operated helicopter. Despite being armed only with an AK-47, the helicopter's crew successfully shot down the An-2, marking the first recorded helicopter victory in air-to-air combat. This event highlighted the ingenuity and unconventional tactics used during the war. However, weeks later, Lima Site 85 was overrun by North Vietnamese forces, resulting in significant U.S. losses.

44406360.article_content:
Defence
Lima Site 85: How a CIA Helicopter Defended a Secret U.S. Radar Facility
During the Vietnam War, a CIA-operated Bell 205 helicopter made history by shooting down a modified North Vietnamese An-2 bomber near Lima Site 85, a secret U.S. radar facility in Laos. This event, marked by ingenuity and daring, showcased the unconventional warfare tactics that defined the conflict
20 de enero de 2025 - 14:34
Ads
In the history of
covert military operations
, few incidents match the audacity and engineering of the shootdown of a modified North Vietnamese An-2 transport plane converted to a bomber by a CIA-operated helicopter in Laos. This event occurred during the Vietnam War, a conflict marked by
unconventional warfare
and daring missions.
Ads
The stage for this incident was
Lima Site 85
, a secret United States Air Force radar installation located atop Phou Pha Thi, a remote mountain in northeastern Laos.
Established in 1966,
Lima Site 85
was crucial for guiding bombing missions over North Vietnam. Operated in secrecy and defended by CIA-backed forces, including Hmong irregular troops, the site’s existence was shrouded in layers of secrecy.
Lima Site 85
played a key role in the U.S. bombing campaign against North Vietnam due to its strategic location and advanced radar technology. The installation featured the AN/TSQ-81 radar system, part of the innovative
Commando Club
program.
This radar enabled
precision-guided bombing
in all weather conditions, a critical capability in a conflict where poor visibility often hindered air operations. By directing attacks, the radar significantly increased the effectiveness of U.S. bombing campaigns against key North Vietnamese targets.
Ads
In addition to the AN/TSQ-81, the site employed a
tactical air navigation (TACAN) system
, providing navigation assistance to combat aircraft operating in the region. The combination of these technologies made
Lima Site 85
indispensable to U.S. military operations, rendering it one of the most valuable and vulnerable facilities in the theater of war.
The attack
On a tense morning in early 1968, a
North Vietnamese Army (NVA) An-2
approached
Lima Site 85
, aiming to disrupt operations and test the defenses of the highly classified installation. The An-2, a tactical transport biplane, was modified to deliver munitions and supplies through floor openings in its cabin, making it a versatile tool for the NVA.
It was armed with
57 mm folding-fin rocket launchers
capable of 12 shots under each lower wing, along with
20 rounds of 250 mm mortar bombs
equipped with aerial bomb fuzes, placed in vertical tubes in the aircraft's cargo hold.
These bombs were dropped through holes cut into the cargo hold floor. Simple hinged bomb bay doors covered these holes during flight, and the pilot could release the entire bomb load by opening these doors.
As the An-2 approached the site, U.S. personnel detected its presence in the sky. The situation called for immediate action. Given the covert nature of the operation and the lack of conventional military support, the defense of
Lima Site 85
fell to an unconventional force: a
Bell 205 helicopter
operated by Air America, a CIA company.
The Air America Bell 205, a civilian version of the military
UH-1 Iroquois (Huey)
, was not designed for air-to-air combat. However, its crew—experienced pilots and support members—were accustomed to operating in dangerous conditions. As the An-2 approached, the Bell 205 climbed to intercept the enemy aircraft.
Armed only with an
AK-47
, the helicopter’s crew chief faced the daunting task of engaging a much larger An-2. The Bell 205 maneuvered skillfully, exploiting its agility and the biplane’s relatively low speed to close in. At one point, the crew chief found himself in a favorable position and fired from the helicopter’s side door, aiming directly at the An-2’s engines and fuselage.
The shootdown
The sustained fire from the AK-47 proved effective. The bullets struck the biplane, causing critical damage to one of its engines. The transport aircraft, unable to maintain altitude, began to lose control. Moments later, it crashed into Laos’s rugged terrain, marking the
first recorded victory of a helicopter over an airplane in air-to-air combat
.
The shootdown of the An-2 highlighted the ingenuity and determination of the personnel defending
Lima Site 85
. Despite inherent risks and equipment limitations, they successfully neutralized a significant threat. This event underscored the
unconventional tactics
employed during the Vietnam War and the unique challenges faced by those operating in covert environments.
The significance of
Lima Site 85
became even more evident weeks later when the site was overrun by North Vietnamese forces in a dramatic and costly assault. The loss of
Lima Site 85
represented the greatest ground combat personnel loss for the U.S. Air Force during the war and underscored the vulnerability of remote installations in hostile territories.

data.title: Arrests of scientists over smuggled samples add to US border anxiety
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 美国边境执法部门近期对携带未申报生物材料的国际科研人员加强了执法，多名外国科学家面临刑事指控。其中包括在哈佛医学院工作的俄罗斯生物信息学家Kseniia Petrova，她因试图走私青蛙胚胎被起诉，并在拘留116天后交保释放。另一案例涉及中国学者Yunqing Jian和Zunyong Liu，他们因涉嫌走私有害真菌而被捕。这些事件引发了科研界对美移民政策收紧和科研环境恶化的担忧。尽管每年都有类似海关违规事件发生，但在特朗普政府下，媒体和执法部门的关注度增加，导致案件被高度曝光。科研人员需严格遵守生物材料的运输规定，以避免法律问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国国土安全部对实验室常用生物秀丽隐杆线虫（C. elegans）的指控是否合理，以及边境管控政策的合理性。

不同观点：
• [质疑观点] perihelions认为，一位密歇根大学的博士研究人员因持有C. elegans被捕和起诉令人难以置信，尤其是考虑到C. elegans是一种常用于实验室的模式生物，而非有害寄生虫。该评论者质疑国土安全部将其描述为对美国农场的国家安全威胁，认为这种指控并不合理。

• [政策担忧] seatac76对边境管控政策的随意性和潜在的焦虑制造表示担忧，暗示这类事件可能会不必要地增加公众的不安，尤其是在指控涉及科学研究材料时。

• [支持管控] readthenotes1则从政府角度出发，认为担心有人携带生物武器入境，包括入侵物种，是合理的，并以入侵植物葛藤（kudzu）为例，说明入侵物种对生态系统的潜在威胁。

US border agents use trained dogs to detect concealed food and biological materials in the luggage of international travelers.  Credit: Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty
After being charged last month with
trying to smuggle frog embryos into the United States
, Kseniia Petrova, a Russian bioinformatician, was indicted on 25 June on additional charges by a grand jury in Boston, Massachusetts — including making a false statement to customs agents. Petrova is one of at least four foreign scientists facing criminal charges for attempting to bring biological material into the country, adding to the
anxiety rippling through the research community
as the administration of US President Donald Trump
slashes science spending
and
cracks down on immigration
.
International PhD students make emergency plans in fear of US immigration raids
Nature
talked to research and legal specialists to understand whether these cases cropping up is unusual and how lab materials should be transported. Detentions for carrying undocumented biological material into the United States happen every year, says Jonathan Grode, an attorney at the immigration law firm Green and Spiegel in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, who is not involved in any of the cases.
Typically, if a person enters the country with a non-hazardous item that is either prohibited or lacks the proper documentation, the authorities confiscate the item, inform the individual of the proper procedure to retrieve it and issue a fine for failing to follow protocol, Grode says. If something is considered hazardous, that changes the calculus, as does being a repeat offender. If you’re both of those things “you are going to get arrested, you are going to be fined and you are going to be denied entry to the country”, he adds.
“The rules have not changed” under the Trump administration, Grode says. What has is the “sensationalism” around any foreigner who has problems at the border, whether from the media or from the Trump team highlighting the case in its deportation efforts, he adds.
Customs violations
Petrova, who had been working at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, was arrested in February for allegedly failing to declare the embryos when transporting them to Harvard from France. At a hearing on 18 June, Brian Goldsworthy, an agent for the US Department of Homeland Security, testified that border agents at Boston’s Logan International Airport asked Petrova whether she had food in her bag and she said no — but she was actually carrying a foam box containing the embryos.
Petrova’s immigration attorney, Gregory Romanowsky, contends that border agents broke protocol, because the alleged customs violation should have triggered a civil process rather than a criminal one. Instead, agents treated the issue as an immigration violation, revoked Petrova’s visa and started deportation proceedings, he says. She spent 116 days in detention before her release from federal custody on bail on 12 June.
Kseniia Petrova was released on bail from federal custody on 12 June.
Credit: Leah Willingham/AP Photo/Alamy
Petrova might be able to avoid some of the criminal charges, because there are questions about whether the embryos were hazardous, Grode says, but her mistake was not to tell the authorities about the embryos in the first place. “That is the number-one way you can find yourself in trouble,” he says.
In another case, the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) arrested Yunqing Jian, a Chinese postdoctoral fellow at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, earlier this month. According to court documents, in July last year, her partner, Zunyong Liu, a researcher at Zhejiang University in China, tried to bring samples of a fungus known as
Fusarium graminearum
, which can harm cereal crops such as wheat, into the United States. He initially denied carrying the fungus in his backpack, the documents say, but then admitted he was taking it to Jian’s university, where he said he planned to study it during his visit. Following an investigation by the FBI, both plant pathologists have been charged with conspiracy, smuggling and making false statements, and Liu has also been charged with visa fraud. Jian remains in custody in Detroit, Michigan.
According to a criminal complaint filed by FBI agent Edward Nieh on 2 June, phone records show that this wasn’t the first time Jian and Liu had smuggled biological materials into the United States.
‘Another blow’: how Trump’s latest travel ban could harm research
On 8 June, another Chinese scientist, Chengxuan Han, was arrested at Detroit Metropolitan Airport. Han, a biologist at Huazhong University of Science and Technology in Wuhan, was planning to spend a year conducting research at the University of Michigan, according to a criminal complaint filed as part of the case. data.title: LLMs Bring New Nature of Abstraction
data.author: hasheddan
data.article_summary: Martin Fowler探讨了生成式AI，尤其是大型语言模型（LLMs），对软件开发的深远影响。他认为，LLMs带来的变革堪比从汇编语言到高级编程语言的转变，但这次不仅是抽象层次的提升，还引入了非确定性工具的编程问题。过去，高级语言（如Ruby）使编程变得更加直观和高效，但本质上仍是以传统方式与机器对话。而LLMs的非确定性特性意味着，使用提示词与机器交互将带来根本性变化，每次输出的结果可能不同，无法通过版本控制确保一致性。这种非确定性是软件开发历史上前所未有的，虽然带来挑战，但也蕴含着尚未被完全理解的机遇，令人兴奋。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕LLMs（大型语言模型）和自然语言编程的适用性、实现方式及其潜在问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **引用先前的研究和批评**：bwfan123 提到 Dijkstra 早年关于“自然语言编程的愚蠢性”的文章，认为当前对“英语作为编程语言”的炒作应被质疑，并呼吁作者引用相关文献以提供更扎实的讨论基础。

• **自然语言的精确性问题**：agentultra 认为自然语言不够精确，无法用于编程，尤其在语义和底层实现的精确性上存在问题。该评论者对“自然语言编程”持怀疑态度，并暗示人们可能混淆了自动化与自然语言编程的区别。

• **模型的改进方向**：abeppu 提出应将重点从适应LLMs转向让模型本身理解编译和执行，建议通过训练模型在代码文本、中间表示（IR）、字节码等多个层次上进行学习，以提高模型的可靠性。评论者认为当前的LLMs存在如变量不存在或方法调用不匹配等问题，并提出通过增加对代码行为和人类描述的训练来解决这些问题。

• **对非确定性的态度**：ptx 对使用LLMs带来的非确定性表示反对，认为不应为了未知的潜在好处而放弃确定性，表达了对当前趋势的怀疑。

• **对自然语言编程的怀疑**：w10-1 对自然语言编程作为“根本性变革”的说法表示怀疑，认为当前的讨论缺乏具体依据，并质疑所谓“新抽象”和“自然”的特点和来源。

• **重复讨论**：bgwalter 指出该讨论是另一个链接的重复，并提到原讨论正在快速沉没，暗示该话题可能缺乏足够的关注或价值。

• **LLMs生成代码的必要性**：dingnuts 质疑为何LLMs在自然语言编程中需要生成高级语言（HLL）代码，而不是直接生成字节码，提出了对LLMs生成代码方式的改进建议。

• **LLMs的确定性问题**：sgt101 澄清了LLMs的确定性问题，指出LLMs本身是确定性的，但特定硬件（如NVIDIA GPU）上的优化可能导致非确定性结果，强调非确定性是一个可选的设置而非LLMs的固有属性。

补充讨论：
• **对自然语言编程的争议焦点**在于其精确性和可行性，部分评论者认为自然语言不够精确，无法替代传统编程语言。
• **对LLMs的改进建议**主要集中在模型对代码的理解和编译过程的参与上，通过多层次的学习和训练来提高模型的可靠性和准确性。
• **对非确定性的态度分歧**：部分评论者对LLMs带来的非确定性表示担忧，而另一些评论者则指出这种非确定性是可控的。

44375795.article_content:
LLMs bring new nature of abstraction
Martin Fowler
24 June 2025
generative AI
Like most loudmouths in this field, I've been paying a lot of attention
to the role that generative AI systems may play in software development. I
think the appearance of LLMs will change software development to a similar
degree as the change from assembler to the first high-level programming
languages. The further development of languages and frameworks increased our
abstraction level and productivity, but didn't have that kind of impact on
the
nature
of programming. LLMs are making that degree of impact, but with
the distinction that it isn't just raising the level of abstraction, but
also forcing us to consider what it means to program with non-deterministic
tools.
High-Level Languages (HLLs) introduced a radically new level of abstraction. With assembler I'm
thinking about the instruction set of a particular machine. I have to figure
out how to do even simple actions by moving data into the right registers to
invoke those specific actions. HLLs meant I could now think in terms of
sequences of statements, conditionals to choose between alternatives, and
iteration to repeatedly apply statements to collections of data values. I
can introduce names into many aspects of my code, making it clear what
values are supposed to represent. Early languages certainly had their
limitations. My first professional programming was in Fortran IV, where âIFâ
statements didn't have an âELSEâ clause, and I had to remember to name my
integer variables so they started with the letters âIâ through âNâ.
Relaxing such restrictions and gaining block structure (âI can have more
than one statement after my IFâ) made my programming easier (and more fun)
but are the same kind of thing. Now I hardly ever write loops, I
instinctively pass functions as data - but I'm still talking to the machine
in a similar way than I did all those days ago on the Dorset moors with
Fortran. Ruby is a far more sophisticated language than Fortran, but it has
the same ambiance, in a way that Fortran and PDP-11 machine instructions do
not.
Thus far I've not had the opportunity to do more than dabble with the
best Gen-AI tools, but I'm fascinated as I listen to
friends and
colleagues
share their experiences. I'm convinced that this is another
fundamental change: talking to the machine in prompts is as different to
Ruby as Fortran to assembler. But this is more than a huge jump in
abstraction. When I wrote a Fortran function, I could compile it a hundred
times, and the result still manifested the exact same bugs. Large Language Models introduce a
non-deterministic abstraction, so I can't just store my prompts in git and
know that I'll get the same behavior each time. As my
colleague
Birgitta put it
, we're not just moving
up
the abstraction levels,
we're moving
sideways
into non-determinism at the same time.
illustration: Birgitta BÃ¶ckeler
As we learn to use LLMs in our work, we have to figure out how to
live with this non-determinism. This change is dramatic, and rather excites
me. I'm sure I'll be sad at some things we'll lose, but there will also
things we'll gain that few of us understand yet. This evolution in
non-determinism is unprecedented in the history of our profession.

data.title: Microsoft extends free Windows 10 security updates into 2026
data.author: jmsflknr
data.article_summary: Microsoft宣布，Windows 10用户可以通过几种方式在官方支持终止后继续获得安全更新。除了支付每年30美元的费用外，用户还可以通过使用Windows Backup应用或花费1000个Microsoft Rewards点数来获得额外一年的安全更新。这些选项不改变Windows 10的官方支持结束日期，但为不想或无法升级到Windows 11的用户提供了额外一年的免费更新。消费者将在今年7月通过通知和设置应用收到相关提示，企业用户则需付费获取最长三年的更新支持。使用Microsoft账户是参与这些计划的必要条件，但一旦注册成功，即便不再使用Windows Backup或退出Microsoft账户，更新仍会继续。微软仍鼓励用户最终升级到Windows 11。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软Windows 10向Windows 11过渡的努力及其相关问题

不同观点：
• **Windows 10过渡到Windows 11的成功与否**：
   - [eviks] 认为微软的努力未见显著成效，因为Windows 10仍有53%的市场份额，接近支持终止时仍有大量用户未升级，这表明微软的推广失败。
   - 隐含的观点认为，Windows 10的用户基数自然减少是升级率低的原因之一，而不仅仅是微软推广不力。

• **Windows 11的使用体验**：
   - [KronisLV] 认为Windows 11在某些方面有改进（如多GPU支持），但也有一些缺点（如垂直任务栏被移除）和问题（如无法安装更新）。
   - 提到Linux在游戏性能上逐渐追赶，并考虑转向Linux，但受限于特定软件和游戏的兼容性。

Last fall, Microsoft
announced
that individuals who wanted to keep using Windows 10 past
its official end-of-support date
could do so by opting into the company's Extended Security Update (ESU) program at a cost of $30 per PC. That payment would get users a single year of additional security updates. Today, less than four months before that October 14, 2025, cutoff, Microsoft is announcing additional options for people who can't or don't want to pay that fee.
Individuals who want to pay $30 for the additional year of updates will still be able to do so. But Microsoft will also extend a year of additional Windows 10 security updates to any users who opt into
Windows Backup
, a relatively recent Windows 10 and Windows 11 app that backs up some settings and files using a Microsoft account. Users can also opt into ESU updates by spending
1,000 Microsoft Rewards points
, which are handed out for everything from making purchases with your Microsoft account to doing Bing searches.
These offers don't formally extend the end-of-support date for Windows 10. But for users who don't want to move to Windows 11 or who can't do so because their PC doesn't meet the requirements, they do effectively offer an additional year of free updates for the OS that's still installed on a slim majority of the world’s Windows PCs,
according to Statcounter data
.
Microsoft's
blog post
says that Windows 10 users will be offered access to the ESU program proactively via notifications and the Settings app. Given how aggressively Microsoft has used these and other means to push Windows 11 upgrades and
new Copilot+ PCs
, it's at least nice that the company isn't making Windows 10 users go digging to keep getting updates. Microsoft will test these notifications in the Windows Insider Preview channel for Windows 10 starting today. They'll begin appearing for regular Windows 10 users in July and should be rolled out to all Windows 10 PCs "by mid-August."
Once enrolled, the ESU program will support consumer Windows 10 PCs until October 13, 2026. Businesses, schools, and other organizations can still get up to three years of ESU updates, but they'll have to pay for the privilege; the year of free-ish updates only applies to consumer PCs. Microsoft said recently that it plans to support the Microsoft 365 and standalone versions of the Microsoft Office apps on Windows 10
until 2028
.
Free* updates
It's worth noting that the Windows Backup and Microsoft Rewards methods for getting these updates require the use of a Microsoft Account, something Microsoft has been pushing with slowly increasing intensity in Windows 11. Windows 10 pushed Microsoft Account usage in various ways, too, but it was generally easier to create and sign in with a local account; for those people, the "free" update offer seems like another effort from Microsoft to bring them into the fold.
The Windows Backup option seems intended to ease the migration to a new Windows 11 PC when the time comes. The company may be offering a short reprieve for Windows 10 users, but the goal is still to shift them to Windows 11 eventually.
"To help make your move to a Windows 11 PC, as simple and secure as possible, we recommend using Windows Backup—built right into Windows 10," writes Microsoft Consumer Chief Marketing Officer Yusuf Medhi in Microsoft's blog post. "It’s an easy way to help you safely and securely transfer your data, personal files, and most settings and applications, so everything’s ready for you the moment you sign in."
People with existing Microsoft Accounts who don't want to use Windows Backup may already have the 1,000 Microsoft Rewards points you would need to enroll in the ESU program; my Microsoft account has 3,411 points attached to it for some reason despite an 18-month expiration window and even though I’ve never taken any intentional steps toward earning any. Users creating a new account for the first time can
accumulate that many points fairly trivially
over the course of a few days, including by downloading the Bing app and doing various Bing searches.
A Microsoft spokesperson confirmed to Ars that Microsoft Account sign-in will be required to enroll a PC into the ESU program. If you reset or reinstall a fresh copy of Windows on a new Windows 10 PC, you'll need to sign back in with a Microsoft account to re-enroll the PC in the ESU program.
But "once a Windows 10 PC is enrolled in ESU, it remains enrolled in the program," the Microsoft spokesperson told Ars. Once enrolled, if you sign out of your Microsoft Account, or if you stop using the Windows Backup app, your PC will continue to receive the security updates afterward.
It’s still the “year of the Windows 11 PC refresh”

data.title: Jane Street's sneaky retention tactic
data.author: yawaramin
data.article_summary: Jane Street, a hedge fund, has adopted a unique tactic to retain its employees by using an obscure, French-based programming language and developing a custom compiler. This unconventional approach not only differentiates the firm but also creates a technical barrier that makes it harder for employees to leave, as their specialized skills may not be as valuable elsewhere. This strategy highlights the extreme measures hedge funds are willing to take in pursuit of profit and competitive advantage. The article also mentions other topics such as tax-avoidance strategies for stocks, the impact of reduced migration, and trends in commodities and prediction markets.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Jane Street使用OCaml语言的利弊及对招聘和工程实践的影响

不同观点：
• **OCaml对招聘的利弊**：
   - **markasoftware**：认为在2025年，OCaml对Jane Street的帮助有限，反而可能阻碍招聘。虽然使用小众语言可以吸引对编程语言有热情的应聘者，但如今Jane Street的规模扩大，多数员工并非因为OCaml加入，而是尽管有OCaml仍选择加入。公司通过高薪和良好的办公环境吸引一般聪明的CS学生，并通过短期训练营让他们适应OCaml。
   - **diekhans**：不同意上述观点，认为有热情的程序员会因为对OCaml的热爱而留下，并且OCaml程序员在应聘Python或C岗位时具有优势。

• **编程语言与生产力的关系**：
   - **mpalmer**：指出优秀的程序员能在几乎任何语言中保持高效，领域经验比语言本身更重要。
   - **nesarkvechnep**：强调Jane Street的工程师是软件工程师，而不仅仅是OCaml开发者，他们的智力水平和能力可能高于一般开发者。

• **OCaml作为技术选择的原因**：
   - **jxjnskkzxxhx**：认为Jane Street使用OCaml并非策略性选择，而是因为技术负责人个人喜好和项目的成功，之后没有理由更换语言。
   - **dmillar**：提到高盛也有类似做法，开发了自己的语言和工具，尽管很多工程师不愿意使用。

• **OCaml的技术优势**：
   - **b0a04gl**：指出使用OCaml可以将系统规则编码进类型系统，减少对文档和隐性知识的依赖，新员工无需询问过多细节，因为类型系统本身限制了错误代码的编写。

• **其他类比**：
   - **scarface_74**：将Jane Street的情况类比为Epic Systems及其使用的Mumps语言。

• **个人观点**：
   - **rapind**：幽默地提到自己使用Elm语言作为保留策略，但仅对自己有效。
   - **odyssey7**：认为如果能避免在机器学习任务中使用Python，使用OCaml是值得的。

• **对文章的批评**：
   - **joshmarinacci**：认为《经济学人》的文章内容浅薄，作为长期订阅者感到失望。

补充讨论：
- 有人提到在法国高等教育中学习OCaml的经历，认为OCaml在实现数学理论方面非常实用，但在留住大学人才方面效果不佳。
- 链接分享（melling）未提供具体讨论内容，但可能指向相关资料。

争议焦点：
- Jane Street使用OCaml是否对招聘和员工保留产生积极或消极影响。
- OCaml作为小众语言，是否能为公司带来长期的技术优势。

data.title: What makes Europe better than America?
data.author: zeroonetwothree
data.article_summary: 文章通过对比作者在美国和意大利用餐的不同体验，反映了美国与欧洲在文化和价值观上的差异。美国注重物质财富、机会和个人自由，而欧洲更重视社区健康、共享资源和地方归属感。作者描述了在意大利一个普通广场享受的美味早餐，以及随后在美国亚特兰大机场附近一家连锁酒店经历的乏味用餐体验，指出这种对比体现了更深层次的文化差异：欧洲的生活方式更具美学和情感上的满足感，而美国则偏向实用和效率，牺牲了环境的美感和个人体验。文章强调，这种差异不仅仅是物质上的，而是价值观和生活态度的不同。

主要讨论点：欧美生活方式的对比以及迁移的考虑

• [amai] 认为欧洲有一些金钱买不到的独特魅力，通过富人选择在欧洲结婚来说明这一点。
• [elvin_d] 赞同amai的观点，并以法国为例，强调欧洲生活质量高。但指出非母语人士面临学习新语言的困难，语言障碍限制了流动性，并成为融入当地社区的主要障碍。
• [rrgok] 持相对中立或消极态度，认为每个地方都有其自身的问题，没有明确偏向欧美任何一方。
• [somewhereoutth] 用幽默的方式将美国比喻为“一场失控的欧洲露营旅行”，指出美国在公共设施和法治方面的问题，暗示欧洲更适合“回家”。
• [basisword] 持平衡观点，认为欧美各有优劣，且随着年龄和生活阶段的变化，个人对居住地的偏好也会改变。强调欧洲有更好的工作与生活平衡、公共交通和医疗保障，而美国可能更适合年轻时追求创业和财富积累。
• [01HNNWZ0MV43FF] 关注实际迁移中的经济与情感障碍，认为由于经济限制和需要离开亲人，迁移到欧洲并不现实。

Recently, on the last morning of a trip to Italy, I found myself in a quiet suburb of Milan. Determined to get food before the long maze of international travel began, I headed to the plaza at 6 a.m—the plaza with the 600-year-old Renaissance sanctuary, that is, not the one with the 500-year-old baroque basilica—to try and find something, anything really, to eat.
The café there wasn’t anything special by Italian standards, but to me as an American, it was outstanding: a display of fresh pastries and croissants, and an array of fruits, eggs, and sandwiches. Since it was my final day, I splurged and let the waitress-owner pick a sugary raisin pastry for me, and for the next hour, I sipped cappuccinos in the cobblestone square, watching the regulars come and go.
Thanks to the delays and incompetence of Delta Air Lines, it would be another 50 hours before I had my next sit-down meal—in the bland lobby of a chain hotel, sitting on an indistinct service road, four miles from the Atlanta airport. That feast—four eggs on two paper plates with plastic silverware and gas station coffee—was five times as expensive. The eggs weren’t that bad, but the setting was bleak: a sterile corporate design meant to keep costs down while offending as few people as possible.
Read
Tyler Cowen: Which Countries Won’t Exist in the 22nd Century?
A crude accounting of cost and calories shows little difference between the two breakfasts, but that’s exactly why such simple measures miss the point. My meal in Italy was uplifting; the one in Atlanta was depressing. The aesthetics of pastries and eggs might seem trivial, but they aren’t—because they point to deeper, more profound differences between two different continents, and two very different cultures.

data.author: belter
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了博通（Broadcom）正悄然通过其网络互连技术争夺AI基础设施市场。虽然GPU在AI中至关重要，但连接这些GPU的网络结构同样关键。博通开发了从可扩展以太网结构到芯片封装内的互连技术，并通过商用芯片和IP授权模式，向各大公司（如谷歌和苹果）提供这些技术。与Nvidia不同，博通专注于 merchant silicon，允许超大规模企业专注于核心逻辑开发，而非互连技术。博通的Tomahawk 5和Tomahawk 6高性能以太网交换机支持大规模GPU集群连接，同时推动以太网在机架规模架构中的应用。此外，博通还投资于共封装光学（CPO）技术，以实现更大、更高效的网络。

44404907.article_content:
Datacenter Networking Nexus
2
How Broadcom is quietly plotting a takeover of the AI infrastructure market
2
When AI is a nesting doll of networks, so why reinvent the wheel when you can license it instead
Tobias Mann
Fri 27 Jun 2025
//
20:49 UTC
feature
GPUs dominate the conversation when it comes to AI infrastructure. But while they're an essential piece of the puzzle, it's the interconnect fabrics that allow us to harness them to train and run multi-trillion-parameter models at scale.
These interconnects span multiple domains, whether it be die-to-die communications on the package itself, between the chips in a system, or the system-to-system networks that allow us to scale to hundreds of thousands of accelerators.
Developing and integrating these interconnects is no small order. It's arguably the reason Nvidia is the powerhouse it is today. However, over the past few years, Broadcom has been quietly developing technologies that span the gamut from scale-out Ethernet fabrics all the way down to the package itself.
And, unlike Nvidia, Broadcom deals in merchant silicon. It'll sell its chips and intellectual property to anyone, and in many cases, you may never know that Broadcom was involved. In fact, it's fairly well established at this point that Google's TPUs made
extensive use
of Broadcom IP. Apple is also
rumored
to be developing server chips for AI using Broadcom designs.
For hyperscalers in particular, this model makes a lot of sense, as it means they can focus their efforts on developing differentiated logic rather than reinventing the wheel to figure out how to stitch all of them together.
Rooted in switching
Your first thought of Broadcom may be the massive
pricing headache
caused by its acquisition of VMware. But if not, you probably associate them with Ethernet switching.
While the sheer number of GPUs being deployed by the likes of Meta, xAI, Oracle, and others may grab headlines, you'd be surprised just how many switches you need to stitch them together. A cluster of 128,000 accelerators might need 5,000 or more switches just for the compute fabric, and yet more may be required for storage, management, or API access.
To address this demand, Broadcom is pushing out some seriously high radix switches, initially with its 51.2Tbps Tomahawk 5 chips in 2022, and more recently, the 102.4Tbps
Tomahawk 6
(TH6), which can be had with your choice of 1,024 100Gbps SerDes or 512 200Gbps SerDes.
The more ports you can pack into a switch, the higher the radix, and the fewer of them are needed for a given number of endpoints. By our calculations, connecting the same number of GPUs from our earlier example at 200Gbps would require just 750 TH6 switches.
Tomahawk 6's higher radix means it can support up to 128,000 GPUs with just 750 switches in two tier architecture. - Click to enlarge
Of course, this being Ethernet, customers aren't locked into one vendor. At GTC earlier this year, Nvidia
announced
a 102.4Tbps Ethernet switch of its own, and we imagine Marvell and Cisco will have equivalent switches before long.
Scale-up Ethernet
Ethernet is most commonly associated with the scale-out fabrics that form the backbone of modern data centers. However, Broadcom is also positioning switches like the Tomahawk 6 as a sort of short-cut to rack-scale architectures.
If you're not familiar, these scale-up fabrics
provide
high-speed chip-to-chip connectivity to anywhere from eight to 72 GPUs, with designs of as
many as 576
expected by 2027. While small meshes up to around eight accelerators can be achieved using simple chip-to-chip meshes, larger configurations like we see in Nvidia's NVL72 or AMD's Helios reference design require switches.
Nvidia already has its NVLink Switches, and while much of the industry has aligned around Ultra Accelerator Link (UALink), an open alternative, the spec is still in its infancy. The first release just
hit in April
, and dedicated UALink switching hardware has yet to materialize.
Broadcom was an early proponent of the tech, but in the past few months, its name has disappeared from the UALink Consortium website, and it's begun talking up its own scale-up Ethernet (SUE) stack, which is designed to work with existing switches.
Here's a quick breakdown of how Broadcom intends to support rack-scale networks using Ethernet - Click to enlarge
While there are benefits to having a stripped-down built-for-purpose protocol like UALink for these kinds of scale-up networks, Ethernet will not only get the job done, but it has the benefit of being available today.
In fact, Intel is already using Ethernet for both scale-up and scale-out networks on its Gaudi system. AMD, meanwhile, plans to
tunnel
UALink over Ethernet for its first generation of rack-scale systems starting next year.
Lighting the way to bigger, more efficient networks
Alongside conventional Ethernet switching, Broadcom has been investing in co-packaged optics (CPO), going back to the introduction of Humboldt in 2021.

data.title: Uncle Sam wants you – to use memory-safe programming languages
data.author: chriseborowski
data.article_summary: 美国网络安全和基础设施安全局（CISA）与国家安全局（NSA）发布指南，敦促软件开发者采用内存安全编程语言，以减少内存漏洞对国家安全和关键基础设施的威胁。内存安全指语言防止内存管理错误的能力，像Rust、Go、Java等语言具备内存自动管理或编译时检查机制。而广泛使用的C和C++默认不具备内存安全，尽管可以通过最佳实践和工具提升安全性，但仍存在风险。过去十年，内存安全问题引发了严重安全事件，如Heartbleed漏洞。微软和谷歌已开始转向内存安全语言，如Rust。尽管Linux社区和C/C++开发者对转型存在抵触和挑战，报告强调了内存安全语言的长期益处，如提高可靠性和降低安全风险，并建议行业加速转型，如通过DARPA的C至Rust翻译项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：内存安全缺陷的危险性及其在现代计算环境中的适用性

不同观点：
• [bgwalter的观点]  
   - 对安全研究人员多年来对内存安全缺陷的警告持怀疑态度。
   - 认为Alex Gaynor虽然提出内存安全问题，但其本人更多是技术圈内的"鼓吹者"（evangelist），而非实际贡献代码的人。
   - 质疑Gaynor的资历，并指出他曾经在不同技术社区中以不同身份出现（Python开发者、PyPy和Rust支持者），暗示其技术立场不够坚定。
   
• [UltraSane的观点]  
   - 认为C语言的内存模型在过去可能有其合理性，但在现代互联网环境中，这种不安全的模型（如缓冲区溢出问题）会带来严重安全隐患。
   - 强调现代计算环境的变化，特别是互联网的普及和服务器安全的重要性，认为继续依赖不安全的C内存模型是灾难性的。

补充讨论：
- bgwalter对Alex Gaynor的个人背景和立场提出质疑，暗示其在技术圈内更多扮演宣传角色而非实际贡献者，这可能涉及到对"技术布道者"和实际开发者角色的讨论。
- UltraSane则专注于技术本身的缺陷，特别是C语言内存模型在现代环境中的不适用性，强调了内存安全漏洞可能带来的实际风险。
- 争议的焦点可能在于对技术人物的多重身份和立场的不信任，以及对内存安全问题严重性的认识差异。

44406339.article_content:
Devops
24
Uncle Sam wants you – to use memory-safe programming languages
24
'Memory vulnerabilities pose serious risks to national security and critical infrastructure,' say CISA and NSA
Thomas Claburn
Fri 27 Jun 2025
//
20:10 UTC
The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the National Security Agency (NSA) this week published guidance urging software developers to adopt memory-safe programming languages.
"The importance of memory safety cannot be overstated," the inter-agency
report
[PDF] says.
The importance of memory safety cannot be overstated
Memory safety refers to the extent to which programming languages provide ways to avoid vulnerabilities arising from the mishandling of computer memory. Languages like Rust, Go, C#, Java, Swift, Python, and JavaScript support automated memory management (garbage collection) or implement compile-time checks on memory ownership to prevent memory-based errors.
C and C++, two of the most widely used programming languages, are not memory-safe by default. And while developers can make them safer through diligent adherence to best practices and the application of static analysis tools, not everyone deploys code with that much care.
To further complicate matters, code written in nominally safe languages may still import unsafe C/C++ libraries using a Foreign Function Interface, potentially breaking memory safety guarantees.
In the past decade, security researchers have been sounding the alarm about the dangers of memory safety flaws. "Memory unsafety is a scourge plaguing our industry,"
said
security researcher Alex Gaynor back in 2017.
Google and Microsoft have attributed the majority of vulnerabilities in large software projects to memory safety errors. In Google's Android operating system, for example,
90 percent
of high-severity vulnerabilities in 2018 came via memory safety bugs. In 2021, the Chocolate Factory
noted
that more than 70 percent of serious security issues in Chromium came from memory safety flaws.
The infamous
Heartbleed flaw
in the OpenSSL cryptographic library was the result of a memory safety error (an out-of-bounds read) in C code. And there are many other examples, including the mid-June
Google Cloud outage
, which Google's incident
report
attributes to a lack of proper error handling for
a null pointer
.
Within a few years, the tech industry began answering the call for memory-safe languages. In 2022, Microsoft executives began calling for new applications
to be written in memory-safe languages like Rust
. By 2023, Consumer Reports – a mainstream product review publication –
published a report on memory safety
and government officials like Jen Easterly, CISA's director at the time, cited the need
to transition to memory-safe languages
during public appearances.
Back in black: Microsoft Blue Screen of Death is going dark
Gridlocked: AI's power needs could short-circuit US infrastructure
Top AI models - even American ones - parrot Chinese propaganda, report finds
Anthropic: All the major AI models will blackmail us if pushed hard enough
The memory safety push created some turmoil in the Linux kernel community over the past year, as efforts to integrate Rust-based drivers
met resistance from kernel maintainers
. And it has
alarmed the C/C++ communities
, where developers have been busily trying to come up with ways to match the memory safety promises of Rust through projects like
TrapC
,
FilC
,
Mini-C
, and
Safe C++
.
The CISA/NSA report revisits the rationale for greater memory safety and the government's calls to adopt memory-safe languages (MSLs) while also acknowledging the reality that not every agency can change horses mid-stream.
Several benefits, such as increased reliability, reduced attack surface, and decreased long-term costs, make a strong case for MSL adoption
"A balanced approach acknowledges that MSLs are not a panacea and that transitioning involves significant challenges, particularly for organizations with large existing codebases or mission-critical systems," the report says. "However, several benefits, such as increased reliability, reduced attack surface, and decreased long-term costs, make a strong case for MSL adoption."
The report cites how Google by 2024 managed to reduce memory safety vulnerabilities in Android to
24 percent of the total
. It goes on to provide an overview of the various benefits of adopting MSLs and discusses adoption challenges. And it urges the tech industry to promote memory safety by, for example, advertising jobs that require MSL expertise.
It also cites various government projects to accelerate the transition to MSLs, such as the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Translating All C to Rust (
TRACTOR
) program, which aspires to develop an automated method to translate C code to Rust.
A recent effort along these lines, dubbed
Omniglot
, has been proposed by researchers at Princeton, UC Berkeley, and UC San Diego. It provides a safe way for unsafe libraries to commu

data.title: Skype Is Gone: The FOSS Alternative
data.author: ekianjo
data.article_summary:
2025年5月5日，Skype在全球范围内关闭，结束了其作为早期互联网音视频通话工具的漫长历史。Skype曾在2004年通过PocketPC实现跨国音频通话，但自2011年被微软收购后逐渐失去 popularity。现在，微软引导用户转向Teams，但其性能缓慢且多bug。

寻找替代软件时，应考虑自由开源软件（FOSS）方案，需满足以下条件：端到端加密、群聊、音视频通话、开放协议、无需电话号码注册、多平台支持、自托管服务器等。

最佳替代方案是Matrix网络及其客户端。Matrix满足上述条件，支持音视频通话、群聊和端到端加密，协议开放，可自托管服务器。然而，Matrix的最佳客户端Element存在一些问题，如移动版客户端账户创建繁琐，新旧版本功能不一致等。此外，Matrix服务器（Synapse）资源消耗较高，但可使用Matrix.org的服务。Matrix组织目前面临财务困难和人员削减问题，未来发展不确定。

44405235.article_content:
On the
5th May 2025
,
Skype
has shut down across the world, ending a very long existence as an
Internet messenger
with audio and video calls capabilities available very early on, before anyone else. I remember very vividly making audio calls from one country to another with
Skype
back in 2004 using my PocketPC (several years before the iPhone). It was a peek into the future of communications, and for a long time there was really nothing like it.
Skype
has progressively lost a lot of popularity following its acquisition with
Microsoft
back in 2011 (hardly surprising…), losing its P2P infrastructure along the way, and it’s now gone for good.
Microsoft
wants you to jump onto
Teams
, which is an even worse choice! Slow, clunky, full of bugs. And SLOW.
Most of you may be already using something else, but in case you are wondering where to go next, and you’d like to consider software that is likely not going away anytime soon, FOSS alternatives should be on the table.
There are many options, but I’m going to set a very specific set of criteria to meet for an application to be considered. Here goes:
End to End encryption for all your messages (that’s expected nowadays)
Group chat (encrypted as well)
Audio calls
Video calls
Open and documented protocols (allowing different clients)
Not relying on a phone number as an ID (Bye Bye Signal and your fake privacy)
FOSS Clients available for all platforms (at least Linux, Windows, Mac, IOS and Android)
Clients working well with each others
Servers that you can host by yourself
It turns out that this list will narrow down the list very, very quickly. In reality, your options are actually quite few. Since it took me quite a lot of time to test different things, I will present you first with the best solution. And afterwards we will review why other options did not make it.
One more thing: I am well aware that
Skype
was also used to make calls to landlines and mobile phones across borders, but this is a feature that is hard to replicate, and somewhat of an add-on. If you need that kind of feature, you will have to rely on other apps on phone or websites that propose such services. Consider this out of scope for the present discussion.
Best Alternative: Matrix Network and Its Clients
We have been using the
Matrix
network at
Boiling Steam
for years now, so we have quite some experience already. All the conditions above are met. You can do audio, video calls, E2E is supported if you want it, there is the concept of group chats, the protocol is open and well documented, you can create accounts using an email address, there are clients for all platforms, and you can host your own Matrix relay or server as well.
All good, right?
Well, on paper, yes, but the reality is more nuanced.
There are some issues that are worth pointing out. For
Matrix
, the best and more featureful clients are
Element
for both desktop and mobile - but the mobile version is now split between the legacy client, the original
Element
, and a new client (developed in Rust) that they are still developing,
Element-X
.
Element-X
uses a newer version of the protocol that supposedly accelerates the synchronization of messages, but in reality it’s hardly working as expected, and has almost zero features compared to the original
Element
client. Since many people are not giving up on
Element
until there is feature parity, the team behind
Element
has now to keep both clients alive. Not ideal.
So, in a normal world, I’d recommend people to start with the legacy
Element
client, but the folks behind
Element
have lost their mind and decided to prevent people from creating new accounts with the legacy
Element
client on mobile.
This means you need to use a computer to create an account in the first place, and then use the legacy
Element
client on phones to be able to log in. Since
Matrix
requires you to verify the validity of each client, this means you need to verify the account you created in the browser with the mobile account you activate in
Element
, which is really an extra pain in the ass, for no good reason. Decisions like them call for a
facepalm
.
People will tell me that there are many other clients for
Matrix
, but in reality most of them only support a fraction of the features of the original
Element
, and suffer from poor UI choices as well and much less support. But things are always changing, and clients may improve or better clients may emerge down the road.
When it comes to hosting the server part, it can be done, and you can use
Synapse
for that, but it’s well known to be a fairly resource intensive server, so you’ll need a relatively powerful VPS or bare-metal hardware in order to host it. If that’s something you don’t want to worry about at first, you can rely on the
Matrix.org
services.
Since
Matrix
is still in heavy development, how healthy is the organization behind it? Well… not doing so well currently. They were in the red for a long time, and fired half of their staff not too long ago.
Their future

data.title: Sailing the fjords like the Vikings yields unexpected insights
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 实验考古学家Greer Jarrett过去三年一直在瑞典沿维京人的航线航行，使用类似维京船的开放式帆船，总航程超过5000公里。他不仅研究了这些船本身，还发现了挪威沿海的四个可能港口，这些港口可能是维京时期贸易和旅行网络的一部分。他的研究发表在《Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory》上。Jarrett使用复原的传统挪威船进行实验，尽管这些船比维京时期晚800年，但他认为造船技术和航行性能足够相似，可以提供有价值的洞见。他的工作帮助填补了维京航海历史中由于缺乏书面记录而留下的空白。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于维京风格船只的实用性、考古学家的资金筹集、相关历史发现和实验考古学的讨论

不同观点：
• medstrom认为这些维京风格的船起初感觉很脆弱，因为它们非常轻，坐上去时感觉很低，与现代帆船不同。然而，经过实际使用后，发现这些船在波浪中非常稳定，甚至能在大的风浪中表现良好。这说明了通过实际操作扩展舒适区的过程。

• snowwrestler指出，拥有考古学博士学位的人能够通过将非商业性活动（如维京船航行）包装成科学研究来筹集资金。这种能力展示了学术界人士需要像企业家一样寻找资助来源，并认为这种做法非常有创意且必要。

• nsavage通过提及HMS Terror的发现，指出当地因纽特人早就知道该船的位置，而官方宣布的发现只是确认了这一事实，强调了原住民知识在考古发现中的重要性。

• Liquix以一种幽默的方式提到一位科学家用自制工具做实验，虽然实验失败了，但这种探索精神值得赞赏。

• divbzero提到了一集关于实验考古学的NOVA节目，通过实际建造金字塔来探索古埃及人的建造技术，这与讨论的主题有相似之处。

• kzrdude指出应提到Helge/Anne Ingstad，他们在发现L'Anse aux Meadows中起到了重要作用，这是与维京人历史相关的重要地点。

• mlhpdx赞同通过实际操作（如上船航行）可以提出不同的问题，强调实践在科学研究中的价值。

• vintermann认为这些船更像Jekt贸易船而非维京船，并指出关于Jekt贸易的英文资料很少。

• zxexz讨论了关于史前人类使用工具的有效性，指出“原始生活”实践者会知道燧石片在屠宰鸟类方面的有效性，并对相关研究文章的结论提出质疑。

补充讨论：
• gdubya的评论似乎是一个幽默的游戏引用，与主要讨论主题无直接关系。

争议焦点：
• 关于这些船只是否真正类似于维京船存在不同看法，vintermann认为更像Jekt贸易船。
• zxexz对文章中关于史前工具使用结论的质疑，强调了实践知识的重要性。

Experimental archaeologist Greer Jarrett of Lund University in Sweden has been sailing in the footsteps of Vikings for the last three years.
If you want to learn more about how and where the
Vikings sailed
, making the journey through the fjords yourself in replica boats is a practical, hands-on approach to achieving that end. Greer Jarrett, an archaeologist at Lund University in Sweden, has spent the last three years doing just that, sailing more than 5,000 kilometers along known Viking trade routes in open, spare-rigged clinker boats similar to those used by the Vikings.
Not only has Jarrett learned a great deal about the boats themselves, he also identified four possible havens along the Norwegian coast, part of what may have been a decentralized network that played a crucial role in trade and travel during that period. And those ports are located farther out to sea than other major ports and hubs known to date, according to
a paper
he published in the Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory.
It's just the latest intriguing discovery enabled by the growing field of experimental archaeology, whereby researchers seek to reverse-engineer all manner of ancient technologies. Experimental archaeologists have, for instance,
built their own versions
of Early Upper Paleolithic adzes, axes, and chisels. The resulting fractures and wear enabled them to develop new criteria for identifying the likely functions of ancient tools. Others have tried to
cook like
the Neanderthals,
concluding that
flint flakes were surprisingly effective for butchering birds, and that roasting the birds damages the bones to such an extent that it's unlikely they would be preserved in the archaeological record.
Kent State University's
Metin Eren
has conducted practical experiments to study, for instance, the trajectories of atlatls attached to spears tipped with replica Clovis points, and how their performance compares to javelins used by Neanderthals. He even
fashioned rudimentary blades
out of his own frozen feces to test whether they could cut through pig hide, muscle, and tendon—solely to test a famous anthropological legend about an elderly Inuit man in the 1950s who purportedly did the same to kill and skin a dog, using its rib cage as a makeshift sled to venture off into the Arctic. (It did not work, so myth: busted. But it did snag Eren an
Ig Nobel prize
.)
Taking a hands-on, experimental archaeological approach to studying the Vikings makes sense in light of the dearth of contemporary written sources. "We have a few things written by outsiders, but there's very, very few accounts written or delivered by people from Scandinavia during that period," Jarrett told Ars. "We normally rely on indirect forms of evidence, be that genetics or archaeology or linguistics, which show strong, very frequent connections across maritime areas in the North Atlantic. But because traveling by boat is kind of an archaeologically invisible act, you don't leave any footprints. So we have very little information about the voyages between these points."
The sailing voyages made by Greer Jarrett during the research project, as well as the four possible Viking harbors he identified.
Credit:
Greer Jarrett
Garrett and his crew used four or five different replica boats for their test voyages. Most were built by volunteers, enthusiasts, or students Jarrett had met during his considerable time in the field. They then sailed along the west coast of the Scandinavian Peninsula, a core area of Viking seafaring.
"These are reconstructions of traditional Norwegian boats from the 1800s and early 1900s," said Jarrett. "My idea was, because of this really long-term continuity in traditional boat building practices, especially in Norway, it might be possible to use these later boats which have lots of similarities to try and work out the potentials of where people might have gotten out. It's the idea of suggesting potentials based on practical experience to try and join those dots between the different evidence we have across the Viking world."
That decision has led to some criticism from colleagues because of the enormous gap in time, but Jarrett defends his choice. "The Viking Age ends in the 11th century, and we're talking about boats from 800 years later," he said. "But the construction techniques and the way they are rigged and their general performance characteristics are similar enough. Because this is a project about voyages and not a project about boat building, it seemed like a defensible analogy."
Seeking safe harbor
"On the long-range voyages, we worked in watches of four hours on and four hours off, and that is just about long enough to get some sleep on your off watch, but also just about short enough that you don't get really, really, really cold, which is obviously a risk," said Jarrett. "It was manageable, but we

data.title: Peter Thiel: Elon Musk has given up on Mars
data.author: elsewhen
data.article_summary: 根据Peter Thiel的言论，Elon Musk已放弃殖民火星的愿景。Thiel在《纽约时报》的采访中表示，Musk不再认为火星殖民是一个可行的政治项目，不再将其视为建立新社会的途径。尽管Musk曾雄心勃勃地计划人类在2028年登陆火星，但与Google DeepMind的AI专家Demis Hassabis对话后，他意识到即使前往火星，地球上的政治和社会问题也可能随之而来。Thiel认为，这促使Musk更加专注于地球上的事务，如支持特朗普和应对社会议题。Musk本人也曾发推称“没有地方可去”，暗示他对太空避难的幻想破灭。

Peter Thiel: Elon Musk has given up on Mars
By
Jack Davey
