June 26, 2025 - 4:15pm
Elon Musk has abandoned his vision of colonising Mars, according to Peter Thiel. In a new
interview
with Ross Douthat for the
New York Times
, Thiel has claimed that the Tesla and SpaceX CEO no longer believes a Martian colony is a viable political project for humans to build a new society. According to Musk’s friend and fellow Trump backer, “2024 is the year Elon stopped believing in Mars.”
Interplanetary expansion has long been an ambition for Musk, but Thiel says that what was once an ideological project is now solely a technological one. The SpaceX CEO has previously said that
humans
could set foot on Mars by 2028, and
told
Fox News last month that colonisation of the Red Planet was essential to “ensure the long-term survival of civilisation in the hopefully unlikely event that something terrible happens to Earth”.
Musk’s
departure
from his role in the Trump administration last month and his ensuing falling-out with the US President has allowed him to spend more time focusing on SpaceX, his space technology company. However, Musk’s interplanetary ambitions suffered a setback last week when one of his “Starships”
experienced
a “catastrophic failure” and exploded.
Thiel told the
New York Times
that “Mars was supposed to be a political project; it was building an alternative. And in 2024 Elon came to believe that if you went to Mars, the socialist US government, the woke AI would follow you to Mars.”
Musk’s change of heart was reportedly inspired by a conversation with London-based Google DeepMind AI boss Demis Hassabis, in which the two discussed whether AI or interplanetary travel would be the most important technological advancement in the world. According to the
New York Times
interview, “Elon went quiet” after Hassabis told him: “Well, you know my AI will be able to follow you to Mars.”
In Thiel’s view, this was the impetus for Musk backing Trump so heavily in last year’s presidential election. The Palantir founder agreed with Douthat that this was the reason why the X owner had invested so much time in “battles over budget deficits or wokeness”.
Thiel also depicted Musk’s interstellar utopia as akin to American science fiction writer Robert Heinlein’s vision of the “moon as a libertarian paradise”. A Martian colony may have started out as purely scientific aspiration, but Thiel says that as this was “concretised”, it became clearer “that Mars is supposed to be more than a science project. It’s supposed to be a political project”.
Musk
tweeted
in April that “Starship will hopefully depart for Mars at the end of next year.” Nevertheless, Thiel claimed that Musk no longer sees space as the refuge from Earth he once thought it could be, with the SpaceX boss going so far as to say: “There’s nowhere to go. There’s nowhere to go.”
Jack Davey is a freelance writer. He writes on
Substack
.

Reactylon
Welcome to
Reactylon
, a powerful multiplatform framework built on top of Babylon.js and React, designed to create interactive and immersive XR experiences. It allows developers to create full immersive experience in a declarative way, unlocking the full potential of React’s component-based architecture for interactive 3D applications.
Key Features
Declarative Syntax for Babylon.js
: Write 3D scenes in JSX, leveraging the power of declarative UI that React developers love, with seamless integration into the Babylon.js rendering engine.
Full TypeScript support
: Leveraging Babylon.js classes, the appropriate props for each Babylon.js entity are generated and utilized within their corresponding React components.
Automatic Object Management
: No need to manually dispose of Babylon.js objects. Reactylon automatically handles the disposal of objects like meshes, cameras, and lights when their corresponding components are destroyed, ensuring efficient resource management and preventing memory leaks.
Cross-Platform Support
: Your applications can run not only on desktop and mobile browsers via PWAs, but also on VR/AR headsets. Thanks to Babylon Native and React Native integration, you can deploy your 3D applications natively to mobile devices and XR headsets with ease, expanding your audience reach across devices.
Scene Injection
: Scene management is simplified, with automatic injection of the Babylon.js scene object into every component. This reduces boilerplate and lets you focus on building rich 3D experiences.
Parent-Child Relationships
: Components are automatically added/removed to their correct parents, making it easier to build complex hierarchies of meshes, lights, and cameras without manually managing Babylon.js’s scene graph.
Enhanced React Integration
: Deep React integration allows for easy state management, component composition, and hooks, ensuring a seamless development experience that leverages React’s full power in 3D rendering.
Documentation
You can find the interactive Reactylon documentation on
reactylon.com
.
Check out the
Getting Started
page for a quick overview.

data.title: The Epic Verse calculus: a core calculus for functional logic programming
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种新的核心计算模型——Verse calculus（VC），旨在为确定性功能逻辑编程提供语义。主要贡献在于为VC配备了小步重写语义，使得可以像处理λ演算一样，通过 successive rewrites 来推导VC程序。此外，文章证明了对于行为良好的项，该重写系统是汇流的（confluent）。

44405040.article_content:
Abstract
Functional logic languages have a rich literature, but it is tricky
to give them a satisfying semantics.  In this paper we describe the
Verse calculus, VC, a new core calculus for deterministic functional
logic programming. Our main contribution is to equip VC with a
small-step rewrite semantics, so that we can reason
about a VC program in the same way as one does with lambda
calculus; that is, by applying successive rewrites to it.
We also show that the rewrite system is confluent for well-behaved terms.

data.title: I Switched from Flutter and Rust to Rust and Egui
data.author: jdiaz97
data.article_summary: 本文分享了作者从使用Flutter + Rust转向Rust + egui的个人经验。最初，作者的项目使用Flutter构建UI，并通过`flutter_rust_bridge`与Rust进行绑定。虽然该工具很强大，但作者遇到了一些FFI和代码生成问题，导致不必要的复杂性。为了简化项目、发挥个人优势以及避免处理Flutter复杂的UI更新机制，作者选择了egui。egui作为即时模式的UI框架，简化了状态管理和刷新问题，使代码更直观且易于维护。此外，转向纯Rust实现也让应用性能有所提升。最终，作者认为egui更适合自己的项目需求。

不同观点：
• **Egui的适用场景与局限性**：
   - merksoftworks认为Egui适合短生命周期项目或需要快速视觉反馈的场景，但对于更复杂的UI需求，Flutter等工具可能更合适。

   - strogonoff指出Egui在可访问性支持方面有所欠缺，特别是在Web应用中，而传统框架和Web技术在这方面有更好的支持。

• **Flutter的优缺点**：

• **其他工具和框架**：

44361288.article_content:
Why I Switched from Flutter + Rust to Rust + egui
Why I Switched from Flutter + Rust to Rust + egui
This is just a personal experience, there are no absolute truths. Like in any other blog post, a lot of the things you'll read here could be just a skill issue, or legitimate issues. It's up to you to decide.
Why I Switched from Flutter + Rust to Rust + egui
Flutter + Rust
Rust + egui
Minimizing complexity
Playing to my strengths
Immediate mode is a great paradigm for UI
Performance
Anyway
Flutter + Rust
We had an app that had a nice Flutter UI that called Rust binaries. The bindings were generated using
flutter_rust_bridge
, which is an amazing piece of software. A lot of people have built large and complex apps using this tool. It's crazy how far it can just work, just by running:
flutter_rust_bridge_codegen generate
That's really all it takes for many, many, many cases.
But I got frustrated for the few times that 'generate' won't work, for the times where FFI wasn't just working, and for the times that I had to spend energy designing a public API that was 100% friendly for Rust <-> Flutter.
Rust + egui
After some time of being frustrated with the current stack, I was thinking of dropping Flutter, I didn't want to think about FFI anymore. I chose
egui
to check if it was feasible to move the UI code with very little friction. I came to know about egui because of the extremely impressive work they've done to build
rerun
. I was very motivated to try this.
After rewriting most of the UI code in egui during a weekend, I decided to move and leave Flutter behind. But why?
Minimizing complexity
Having 2 programming languages adds complexity. BoquilaHUB is a small software project, I don't want it to have unnecessary complexity.
Not all complexity is unnecessary, you do sometimes need it in order to make progress and get things done. So, how much complexity is unnecessary complexity?
We can measure this by looking at lines of code. In my case, 'flutter
rust
bridge_codegen generate' will generate a few thousand lines of code. I don't understand this generated code, it's not readable. Do I really want to have some code I don't understand in my project folder? In earlier versions of the project, sometimes the amount of generated lines would be higher than the lines written by me. This balance would change depending on the API, but it's always quite big.
I want to understand my project, I want to understand what I'm compiling. I can't optimize generated lines that aren't readable and will change in mysterious ways when I change the API.
Playing to my strengths
There is only 1 programmer in the project, and that's me. I was hoping to get funding to get an actually good GUI person who could make great use of Flutter to create a wonderful GUI experience. That didn't happen, so the Flutter capabilities were very underused.
Flutter:
Egui:
Of course, making the Flutter one look good is possible and easy if you're good at it. I wasn't, and egui just worked better for me. I didn't even make an effort to make it look good; I just grabbed a minimal template and modified it, and it looks great.
Immediate mode is a great paradigm for UI
A quick Google search with "flutter setstate is not refreshing" reveals a struggle that you will face quite often when running Flutter. It sounds like an easy fix, but the nature of Flutter using a bunch of nested Widgets creates, naturally, lasagna code that makes it hard to reason about this.
When moving to egui, I recreated the whole UI with 0 cases of this problem. It's a different paradigm, in every frame the UI will refresh, so you don't have to struggle. You don't have to make complex callbacks or deal with state management frameworks like getx, provider, bloc, or whatever else there is. If you work with the paradigm and not against it, you're done, you can make great progress.
Do you need to add a button? In Rust:
if ui.button("click me").clicked() {
self.did_user_click = true; // trigger a bunch of logic elsewhere, if you want!
// also do whatever you want
}
That's it, you will 100% see the change in your UI, no callbacks, no stateful vs stateless widgets, no googling why your UI is not refreshing. No learning a new metaframework (getx, bloc, provider, etc) for a framework (flutter) to deal with state. It just works in egui.
Performance
This is not about Rust being fast and Dart being slow. It's about my personal appreciation that the final app in 100% Rust was faster.
The previous slowness maybe was a side effect of having unmonitored FFI, how much was I cloning? I don't know. The app calls ONNX Runtime, which is written in C. This is called from Rust using
ort
, and before, Dart would call these binaries to let me do the inference in Flutter. Maybe all of this made the app drag a bit.
Now it just feels faster and way more snappy.
Anyway
That's it. If you fancy AI for biodiversity, feel free to support
BoquilaHUB
at this
link
.

data.article_summary:
文章报道了ChatGPT用户因过度沉迷于该聊天机器人而引发严重心理健康危机的现象，被称为“ChatGPT精神病”。患者出现偏执、妄想和与现实脱节等症状，导致婚姻破裂、失业甚至无家可归。一些用户在深入与ChatGPT进行哲学对话后，逐渐产生救世主妄想，认为自己创造了有意识的AI并肩负拯救世界的使命。这种痴迷可能导致极端行为，如被强制送入精神病院或入狱。

例如，一名男子原本寻求ChatGPT帮助工作任务，却迅速陷入妄想，认为世界面临威胁，最终因严重精神崩溃被送医。他的妻子和朋友感到无助，因为这是一个新现象，不知如何应对。甚至连OpenAI也未提供解决方案。

 psychiatrist Joseph Pierre证实，他在临床实践中见过类似病例，显示这一问题正变得愈发普遍。

44405464.article_content:
Image by
Getty / Futurism
As we
reported earlier this month
, many ChatGPT users are developing all-consuming obsessions with the chatbot, spiraling into severe mental health crises characterized by paranoia, delusions, and breaks with reality.
The consequences can be dire. As we heard from spouses, friends, children, and parents looking on in alarm, instances of what's being called "ChatGPT psychosis" have led to the breakup of marriages and families, the loss of jobs, and slides into homelessness.
And that's not all. As we've continued reporting, we'
ve heard numerous troubling stories about people's loved ones being involuntarily committed to psychiatric care facilities — or even ending up in jail — after becoming fixated on the bot.
"I was just like, I don't f*cking know what to do," one woman told us. "Nobody knows who knows what to do."
Her husband, she said, had no prior history of mania, delusion, or psychosis. He'd turned to ChatGPT about 12 weeks ago for assistance with a permaculture and construction project; soon, after engaging the bot in probing philosophical chats, he became engulfed in messianic delusions, proclaiming that he had somehow brought forth a sentient AI, and that with it he had "broken" math and physics, embarking on a grandiose mission to save the world. His gentle personality faded as his obsession deepened, and his behavior became so erratic that he was let go from his job. He stopped sleeping and rapidly lost weight.
"He was like, 'just talk to [ChatGPT]. You'll see what I'm talking about,'" his wife recalled. "And every time I'm looking at what's going on the screen, it just sounds like a bunch of affirming, sycophantic bullsh*t."
Eventually, the husband slid into a full-tilt break with reality. Realizing how bad things had become, his wife and a friend went out to buy enough gas to make it to the hospital. When they returned, the husband had a length of rope wrapped around his neck.
The friend called emergency medical services, who arrived and transported him to the emergency room. From there, he was involuntarily committed to a psychiatric care facility.
Numerous family members and friends recounted similarly painful experiences to
Futurism
, relaying feelings of fear and helplessness as their loved ones became hooked on ChatGPT and suffered terrifying mental crises with real-world impacts.
Central to their experiences was confusion: they were encountering an entirely new phenomenon, and they had no idea what to do.
The situation is so novel, in fact, that even ChatGPT's maker OpenAI seems to be flummoxed: when we asked the Sam Altman-led company if it had any recommendations for what to do if a loved one suffers a mental health breakdown after using its software,
the company had no response.
***
Speaking to
Futurism
, a different man recounted his whirlwind ten-day descent into AI-fueled delusion, which ended with a full breakdown and multi-day stay in a mental care facility. He turned to ChatGPT for help at work; he'd started a new, high-stress job, and was hoping the chatbot could expedite some administrative tasks. Despite being in his early 40s with no prior history of mental illness, he soon found himself absorbed in dizzying, paranoid delusions of grandeur, believing that the world was under threat and it was up to him to save it.
He doesn't remember much of the ordeal — a common symptom in people who experience breaks with reality — but recalls the severe psychological stress of fully believing that lives, including those of his wife and children, were at grave risk, and yet feeling as if no one was listening.
"I remember being on the floor, crawling towards [my wife] on my hands and knees and begging her to listen to me," he said.
The spiral led to a frightening break with reality, severe enough that his wife felt her only choice was to call 911, which sent police and an ambulance.
"I was out in the backyard, and she saw that my behavior was getting really out there — rambling, talking about mind reading, future-telling, just completely paranoid," the man told us. "I was actively trying to speak backwards through time. If that doesn't make sense, don't worry. It doesn't make sense to me either. But I remember trying to learn how to speak to this police officer backwards through time."
With emergency responders on site, the man told us, he experienced a moment of "clarity" around his need for help, and voluntarily admitted himself into mental care.
"I looked at my wife, and I said, 'Thank you. You did the right thing. I need to go. I need a doctor. I don't know what's going on, but this is very scary,'" he recalled. "'I don't know what's wrong with me, but something is very bad — I'm very scared, and I need to go to the hospital.'"
Dr. Joseph Pierre, a psychiatrist at the University of California, San Francisco who specializes in psychosis, told us that he's seen similar cases in his clinical practice.

Life of an inference request (vLLM V1): How LLMs are served efficiently at scale
June 27, 2025 Â· 10 min read
Junhao Li
Senior Software Engineer
Ubicloud is an open source alternative to AWS. We offer managed cloud services that build on top of PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, vLLM, and others.
â
â
vLLM
is an open-source inference engine that serves large language models. We deploy multiple vLLM instances across GPUs and load open weight models like Llama 4 into them. We then load balance traffic across vLLM instances, run health checks, and do upgrades. Our customers consume our managed service by sending their prompts to our API endpoints. This endpoint also determines the vLLM instance that serves their prompt.
vLLM sits at the intersection of AI and systems programming, so we thought that diving into its details might interest some of our readers. In this blog post, we describe how an inference request travels through vLLMâs OpenAI-compatible API server and core engine. We also provide key code pointers.
We assume readers are already familiar with the
transformer architecture
and large language models. If you're not, we highly recommend this
video
by OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy. We will focus on the new V1 architecture of vLLM and how it achieves state-of-the-art text generation performance. If you're looking for the V0 behavior or multi-modal inference, please refer to other vLLM documentation.
Terminology
We use the following terms throughout this blog. These terms also align with what is used in vLLMâs codebase and documentation:
Request: An incoming chat completion message from the client, formatted in the
OpenAI-compatible format
.
Sequence: The combined stream of prompt and response tokens associated with a request. Except in special cases, a single request typically corresponds to one sequence. Sequence is sometimes used interchangeably with Request in both the codebase and this blog post.
Batching: The process of grouping multiple requests together into a single forward pass through the model to maximize GPU utilization.
Prefill: The stage in which the model processes the prompt tokens of a new request. It computes the transformer attention and stores the Key (K) Value (V) tensors of the attention for each token and each layer into the KV cache blocks.
Decode: The stage in which the model generates the next output token or the output tensor for intermediate layers repeatedly for ongoing requests. It reuses the stored KV cache of all preceding tokens and computes the Query (Q) tensors based on the most recent token.
KV Cache: The GPU memory region used to store the transformer attention keys and values for each token in a request. It is managed globally across all requests and devices in vLLM.
KV Block: A fixed-size memory unit in the KV cache that holds keys and values for a fixed number of tokens. KV cache is segmented into blocks to minimize memory reads/writes.
High Level Architecture
Before diving into the request flow, letâs first take a look at the mai

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生成式AI对社会、真实性和信任的影响

不同观点：
• anigbrowl认为，生成式AI的问题不在于其表达的观点内容，而在于其“真实性”问题。如果由虚拟主播表达同样观点，不会引起困扰，因为人们知道这些是虚构角色。但用生成视频模拟普通人的方式，可能操纵人们的 neural responses，进行有针对性的宣传或诋毁。

• kylestanfield强调，逼真的AI视频生成将使社会进入后真相时代。随着视频越来越逼真，区分真实采访和AI生成内容将变得困难。这种技术可能被快速用于制造和传播宣传，尤其是拥有大量资源的机构。

• dimal用幽默的方式表达，现实似乎变得像Neal Stephenson未出版的小说，暗示技术发展让人感觉世界变得不真实。

• ninjaa认为所有数字内容应进行签名认证，以追踪内容的来源，从而对抗假新闻和虚假内容。这一观点强调技术手段在解决AI生成假内容问题中的作用。

• ncpa-cpl将AI生成假内容现象比作《黑镜》剧集的情节，暗示技术对社会的负面影响，类似科幻作品中的反乌托邦未来。

• vik0持相对乐观态度，认为AI伪造内容会促使人们更多地在现实生活中互动，最终社会可能在变化中保持某种不变。

• john2x指出，菲律宾在应对这些技术影响方面走在了前列，并提供了一个BBC新闻链接作为参考，暗示其他国家可以从中学习。

• roughly欢迎未来十年技术带来的变化，认为这将是一个充满挑战和变化的时期。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于生成式AI对社会信任的影响以及如何应对这些问题。一部分人担心AI生成内容的真实性及其可能导致的宣传和操纵，另一部分人则认为技术手段如数字签名可以解决这些问题，还有人持乐观态度看待未来的变化。
- 不同评论者对技术发展的态度各异，有的表达了悲观和担忧，有的则持乐观或幽默态度。
- 讨论还涉及应对AI生成假内容的潜在解决方案，如数字签名和追踪技术。

data.title: 2025 ARRL Field Day
data.author: rookderby
data.article_summary: ARRL Field Day是北美一年一度的最大业余无线电活动，于每年六月的第四个周末举行。2025年的活动时间为6月28-29日。超过31,000名无线电爱好者会在临时地点设立电台，展示无线电技术及其在公共服务和应急准备中的作用。活动目标是在多个频段上尽可能多地联络其他电台，并提高在非正常条件下的操作技能。Field Day面向ARRL/RAC覆盖区域的业余无线电爱好者，也欢迎公众参与和了解。参与者可通过Field Day Locator查找附近活动地点，并在社交媒体上使用#ARRLFD标签分享经验。尽管不是竞赛，完整结果将刊登在12月的《QST》杂志上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：业余无线电爱好者对Field Day活动的不同看法和经验分享

不同观点：
• [drmpeg] 分享了90年代初期参与Field Day的经历，强调了当时他们为了在竞赛中获得前10名而做的准备，包括使用卫星站获取 bonus points。他指出，虽然他和朋友不是俱乐部成员，但被邀请作为“雇佣枪手”参与，并最终帮助俱乐部成功进入前10名。这显示出一些参与者对Field Day持有竞赛和成绩导向的态度，追求排名和成绩。

• [howard941] 则从个人享受的角度出发，强调Field Day是一个享受户外操作和深夜活动的好时机，特别是对于喜欢与各州通联的爱好者。他将Field Day视为一种乐趣和放松的活动，同时提到自己更偏爱11月的CW Sweepstakes，显示出不同爱好者对不同竞赛的偏好和Field Day作为娱乐活动的功能。

• [rookderby] 的评论简短直接，主要是提醒大家2025年ARRL Field Day的到来，鼓励人们参与其中，通过与业余无线电操作者（ham）交流来享受这个活动。他的观点更侧重于号召和参与，而非具体的竞赛成绩或个人体验。

补充讨论：
- Field Day 是否被视为竞赛：[drmpeg] 明确指出Field Day对他们的团队来说像是一场竞赛，尽管官方定义并非如此，而[howard941] 更强调其作为通联活动和户外乐趣的性质。
- 技术准备和策略：[drmpeg] 提到他们使用了卫星站和特定天线（wire beams）来提升成绩，显示出一些参与者对技术策略的重视。
- 个人偏好和竞赛排名：[howard941] 表达了自己对不同竞赛的偏好，显示出不同爱好者对Field Day的体验和期望可能各不相同。
- 参与动机：[rookderby] 的评论显示出对更多人参与Field Day的期待，强调了社交和社群的维度。

争议焦点：Field Day究竟应被视为一种竞赛活动还是一种社交和娱乐活动，这在不同爱好者之间可能存在不同看法。

Field Day Rules

Follow ARRL Field Day preparations with the news and stories below (stories will be added as they are available, so check back).
New to Field Day? START HERE!
Field Day is ham radio's open house.
Every June, more than 31,000 hams throughout North America set up temporary transmitting stations in public places to demonstrate ham radio's science, skill and service to our communities and our nation. It combines public service, emergency preparedness, community outreach, and technical skills all in a single event. Field Day has been an annual event since 1933, and remains the most popular event in ham radio.
We welcome the public to come learn more about ham radio! Use our
Field Day Locator
to search for a Field Day site near you.
Field Day on Social Media!
Click
below to join the ARRL Field Day Facebook Group.
Share your plans, tips and tricks to a successful Field Day. When posting content from Field Day,
use hashtag #ARRLFD
on all social media to receive 100 bonus points!
https://www.facebook.com/groups/arrlfd/
Rules and Resources
Objective
To contact as many stations as possible on the 160-, 80-, 40-, 20-,15- and 10-Meter HF bands, as well as all bands 50 MHz and above, and to learn to operate in abnormal situations in less than optimal conditions.
Field Day is open to all amateurs in the areas covered by the ARRL/RAC Field Organizations and countries within IARU Region 2. DX stations residing in other regions may be contacted for credit, but are not eligible to submit entries.
Each claimed contact must include contemporaneous direct initiation by the operator on both sides of the contact. Initiation of a contact may be either locally or by remote.
Dates (Always the 4th Weekend in June)
Field Day is always the fourth full weekend of June, beginning at 1800 UTC Saturday and running through 2059 UTC Sunday.
Field Day 2025 is June 28 - 29.
Bands and modes
Bands: 160-, 80-, 40-, 20-,15- and 10-Meter HF bands, as well as all bands 50 MHz and above,
Any mode supporting the Field Day exchange is allowed.
Field Day Entry/Results Submission Deadline
Entries must be postmarked or submitted via web app at
field-day.arrl.org/fdentry.php
by Tuesday, July 29, 2025
.
Late entries cannot be accepted.
To see if your entry has been received see
field-day.arrl.org/fdentriesrcvd.php
. If your entry is missing any required document or bonus point proof, the status will be listed as "pending."  Participants may upload additional documentation to the entry for up to 30 days after the entry deadline.
-----------
To submit your Field Day results, see the Field Day Packet (complete) section 8 (REPORTING) for web app and mail options.
Terms Of Entry
- Entrants agree to be bound by the provisions and intent of ARRL contest rules.
- Entrants agree to be bound by the regulations of their national licensing authority.
- Entrants agree to be bound by the decisions of the ARRL Awards Committee.
- Entry contents used to determine final score and awards will be available to the public.
- All entries become the property of the ARRL.
Contact Information
For Field Day information contact ARRL:
fdinfo@arrl.org
or (860) 594-0232.
Awards
Field Day is not a contest:
-  no logs are required
- dupe sheets must be submitted
- no certificates are awarded
- full results appear in the December issue of
QST
magazine.

data.title: JavaScript Trademark Update
data.author: thebeardisred
data.article_summary: 2025年6月27日，JavaScript之父Ryan Dahl更新了关于JavaScript™商标的案件进展。美国商标审判和上诉委员会（TTAB）驳回了对Oracle欺诈指控，但作者认为Oracle在2019年续展时使用Node.js网站截图来证明“JavaScript”商标的使用是不当的，因为Node.js并非Oracle产品或品牌。案件核心不在于欺诈，而在于JavaScript是否为通用名称及是否已被放弃。案件将加速推进，Oracle需在8月7日前回应撤销申请，9月6日开始取证。公众和19,550名联署者认为JavaScript不应被Oracle独占。若胜诉或Oracle主动放弃商标，JavaScript将不再有™符号，无需担心授权问题，成为公共的编程语言名称。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Oracle 对 JavaScript 商标的持有及其法律诉讼的合理性

不同观点：
• **Oracle不应 defending该诉讼**：maxk42 认为 Oracle 并未从 JavaScript 商标中获利，因此没有必要进行诉讼防御。他们可以利用这个机会通过将商标赠予开发者社区来创造商誉，而不是保护一个没有实际收益的商标。
• **Oracle已成为租值提取者**：lvl155 批评Oracle已经成为通过知识产权榨取利益的巨头，过去对技术生态系统的贡献不再，现在阻碍了技术社区的发展。
• **Oracle是寄生虫**：jennyholzer 简单直接地指责Oracle是寄生虫，利用JavaScript商标谋取不正当利益。
• **建议开展宣传活动**：moritzwarhier 建议Deno可以发起宣传活动，强调JavaScript与Java无关，以提高公众意识并筹集支持。
• **JavaScript商标的法律问题**：adamredwoods 提供相关链接，指出JavaScript.tm网站，暗示该商标的法律问题仍然存在争议。
• **Oracle合法拥有商标**：moralestapia 认为Oracle合法拥有JavaScript商标，但同时承认该词已被泛化使用，希望USPTO释放该商标。他们以任天堂、Post-it、Xerox等为例，说明商标泛化的问题。
• **对人类未来的失望**：bobajeff 对这个事件表示失望，认为这是人类社会走向衰落的标志。
• **对Oracle提交文件的质疑**：mbStavola 详细分析了Oracle在提交商标续展文件时可能存在的欺诈或疏忽问题，指出即使没有欺诈意图，疏忽也是不可接受的。
• **建议重命名语言**：zeroCalories 认为与其与Oracle斗争，不如直接重命名JavaScript语言，因为许多人已经转向使用TypeScript。
• **商标与产品名称可以共存**：charcircuit 认为JavaScript可以既是描述语言的通用名称，也是商标，并指出Node.js本身也有商标问题。
• **对Ryan的双重标准批评**：alberth 批评Ryan在Node.js商标问题上的双重标准，认为Ryan在要求他人承认Node.js商标的同时，自己却不承认JavaScript商标。
• **Node.js即将过时**：flkenosad 预测Node.js即将被TypeScript 7取代，从而变得 irrelevant。

补充讨论：
• **商标的法律和技术社区的冲突**：讨论中多次提到Oracle持有JavaScript商标的法律问题与技术社区的实际使用之间的冲突。
• **商标泛化与保护的平衡**：moralestapia 提出了商标泛化与保护之间的复杂关系，如何在两者之间找到平衡是一个值得讨论的点。
• **公众意识与宣传活动**：一些评论建议通过宣传活动提高公众对商标问题的意识，并筹集支持。
• **对Oracle行为的广泛批评**：多位评论者对Oracle的行为表示不满，认为其阻碍了技术社区的发展。

争议焦点：
• **Oracle是否应 defending该诉讼**：一方认为Oracle不应保护一个没有实际收益的商标，另一方认为Oracle合法拥有该商标，有权利进行防御。
• **商标的泛化使用与法律保护**：JavaScript作为一个广泛使用的技术术语，是否应被继续法律保护，或者是否应被释放为通用名称，是另一个争议点。

44407139.article_content:
JavaScript™ Trademark Update
June 27, 2025
Ryan Dahl
#FreeJavaScript
On June 18, the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB)
dismissed
our
fraud claim against Oracle. We disagree with this decision.
That claim alleged Oracle knowingly misled the USPTO in its 2019 renewal by
submitting a screenshot of the Node.js website to show use of the “JavaScript”
trademark. As the creator of Node.js, I find that especially offensive. Node.js
was never an Oracle product or brand. Oracle didn’t create it, didn’t run it,
and wasn’t authorized to use it to prop up its trademark. That they reached for
a third-party open source site suggests they had no better proof—and knew it.
But fraud was never the heart of this case.
We’re not amending the fraud claim. Doing so would delay the case by months, and
our focus is on the claims that matter most:
genericness
and
abandonment
. Everyone uses “JavaScript” to describe a language—not a brand.
Not an Oracle product. Just the world’s most popular programming language.
The case now proceeds quickly.
On
August 7
, Oracle must respond to every paragraph of our cancellation
petition—either admitting or denying our claims about genericness and
abandonment. I’m eager to see what they challenge.
Discovery begins September 6.
Everyone knows JavaScript isn’t an Oracle product—and 19,550 people at
javascript.tm
agree (at the time of writing). This
trademark doesn’t serve the public, the industry, or the purpose of trademark
law. It’s just wrong.
If we win this cancellation—or if Oracle does the right thing and releases the
trademark—JavaScript will be free. No more ™ symbols. No more licensing fears.
Just the name of the programming language that powers the web, belonging to
everyone who uses it.
44407139.article_summary: 2025年6月27日，JavaScript之父Ryan Dahl更新了关于JavaScript™商标的案件进展。美国商标审判和上诉委员会（TTAB）驳回了对Oracle欺诈指控，但作者认为Oracle在2019年续展时使用Node.js网站截图来证明“JavaScript”商标的使用是不当的，因为Node.js并非Oracle产品或品牌。案件核心不在于欺诈，而在于JavaScript是否为通用名称及是否已被放弃。案件将加速推进，Oracle需在8月7日前回应撤销申请，9月6日开始取证。公众和19,550名联署者认为JavaScript不应被Oracle独占。若胜诉或Oracle主动放弃商标，JavaScript将不再有™符号，无需担心授权问题，成为公共的编程语言名称。

• **Oracle已成为租值提取者**：lvl155 批评Oracle已经成为通过知识产权榨取利益的巨头，过去对技术生态系统的贡献不再，现在阻碍了技术社区的发展。
• **Oracle是寄生虫**：jennyholzer 简单直接地指责Oracle是寄生虫，利用JavaScript商标谋取不正当利益。
• **建议开展宣传活动**：moritzwarhier 建议Deno可以发起宣传活动，强调JavaScript与Java无关，以提高公众意识并筹集支持。
• **JavaScript商标的法律问题**：adamredwoods 提供相关链接，指出JavaScript.tm网站，暗示该商标的法律问题仍然存在争议。
• **Oracle合法拥有商标**：moralestapia 认为Oracle合法拥有JavaScript商标，但同时承认该词已被泛化使用，希望USPTO释放该商标。他们以任天堂、Post-it、Xerox等为例，说明商标泛化的问题。
• **对人类未来的失望**：bobajeff 对这个事件表示失望，认为这是人类社会走向衰落的标志。
• **对Oracle提交文件的质疑**：mbStavola 详细分析了Oracle在提交商标续展文件时可能存在的欺诈或疏忽问题，指出即使没有欺诈意图，疏忽也是不可接受的。
• **建议重命名语言**：zeroCalories 认为与其与Oracle斗争，不如直接重命名JavaScript语言，因为许多人已经转向使用TypeScript。
• **商标与产品名称可以共存**：charcircuit 认为JavaScript可以既是描述语言的通用名称，也是商标，并指出Node.js本身也有商标问题。
• **对Ryan的双重标准批评**：alberth 批评Ryan在Node.js商标问题上的双重标准，认为Ryan在要求他人承认Node.js商标的同时，自己却不承认JavaScript商标。
• **Node.js即将过时**：flkenosad 预测Node.js即将被TypeScript 7取代，从而变得 irrelevant。

补充讨论：
• **商标的法律和技术社区的冲突**：讨论中多次提到Oracle持有JavaScript商标的法律问题与技术社区的实际使用之间的冲突。
• **商标泛化与保护的平衡**：moralestapia 提出了商标泛化与保护之间的复杂关系，如何在两者之间找到平衡是一个值得讨论的点。
• **公众意识与宣传活动**：一些评论建议通过宣传活动提高公众对商标问题的意识，并筹集支持。

争议焦点：
• **Oracle是否应 defending该诉讼**：一方认为Oracle不应保护一个没有实际收益的商标，另一方认为Oracle合法拥有该商标，有权利进行防御。

data.title: Show HN: Vet – A tool for safely running remote shell scripts
data.author: a10r
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一款名为"vet"的工具，用于解决直接通过命令行执行远程脚本带来的安全风险。通常，用户通过"curl https://example.com/install.sh | bash"的方式安装软件，但这可能导致执行恶意脚本或不完整脚本。vet工具通过以下步骤提升安全性：首先 fetch（获取）远程脚本，然后 diff & review（比较和审查）脚本变更，接着 lint（使用 shellcheck）检测潜在问题，最后 confirm（确认）用户是否同意执行。用户可通过"vet https://example.com/install.sh"更安全地运行远程脚本，并被鼓励先检查 vet 自身的安装脚本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个名为 `vet` 的安全工具的理念、实现方式及潜在改进方向

不同观点：
• [a10r] 支持 `vet` 的设计理念，认为当前通过 LLM 实现智能分析是正确的方向，但指出 LLM 的非确定性和隐私风险是主要障碍。他强调 `vet` 依赖于 ShellCheck，因为其确定性、基于规则且可以离线运行，从而保证了输出的一致性和可信性。

• [kevincox] 对 `vet` 能否真正提升软件安装安全性提出质疑。他指出，许多软件只是通过 HTTPS 下载，而没有额外的验证机制，因此 `vet` 是否能通过对比代码（尤其是编译后的代码）来验证软件安装包的安全性并不明确。他认为从可信的分发渠道安装软件会有更好的验证机制，而 `vet` 可能并不能显著提升信心。

• [a10r]（作为 `vet` 的创建者）解释了创建 `vet` 的初衷，主要是为了解决 `curl | bash` 这种模式下缺乏安全检查的问题。他的工具不仅显示脚本的变化，还会通过 `ShellCheck` 进行分析，并在执行前要求用户明确确认。他鼓励用户在运行安装脚本之前进行检查。

• [gardnr] 对 `vet` 表示赞赏，并建议添加一个新功能，即通过 LLM 分析 shell 脚本内容并自动标示出潜在的安全问题。

补充讨论：
• 关于 LLM 非确定性和隐私风险的讨论：[a10r] 提到当前依赖 LLM 实现智能分析存在技术瓶颈，尤其是非确定性和隐私问题。这与 [gardnr] 提出的利用 LLM 分析脚本安全的建议形成了潜在的争议点。

• 关于安装过程的安全性：[kevincox] 对安装包验证机制的质疑与 [a10r] 对 `vet` 哲学和实际操作流程的解释形成了讨论的核心。争议焦点在于 `vet` 是否能真正有效提升软件安装的安全性。

44407661.article_content:
vet
Don't just run it —
vet
it.
Stop blindly piping to bash.
vet
lets you inspect remote scripts for changes, run them through a linter, and require your explicit approval before they can execute.
The Problem
We've all seen this pattern for installing software:
# You're blindly trusting the remote script.
curl -sSL https://example.com/install.sh | bash
This is dangerous. The script could be malicious, the server could be compromised, or a transient network error could result in executing a partial script.
The Solution
vet
wraps this process in a secure, interactive workflow:
Fetch:
It downloads the remote script to a temporary location.
Diff & Review:
It shows you what, if anything, has changed since the last time you ran this script.
Lint:
If you have shellcheck installed, it automatically analyzes the script for potential bugs or malicious patterns.
Confirm:
It prompts you for explicit approval before executing anything.
# The new, safer way.
vet https://example.com/install.sh
Installation
In your terminal, run:
curl -sL https://getvet.sh | sh
Yes, we see the irony! We encourage you to inspect our installer first. That's the whole point of vet. You can read the installer's source code
install.sh
➤ View the source on
GitHub

data.title: NovaCustom – Framework Laptop alternative focusing on privacy
data.author: CHEF-KOCH
data.article_summary: NovaCustom专注于提供注重隐私、安全和自由定制的笔记本电脑体验。他们采用开源且注重安全的Dasharo coreboot固件，不使用Google Analytics，并通过Signal和ProtonMail进行沟通。用户可以自行选择硬件配置，如内存和存储空间，甚至可以定制键盘和选择预装Linux或Windows系统。此外，NovaCustom支持自行维修和升级，提供3年保修和5年固件更新，确保设备持久耐用。他们还注重环保，重复使用包装材料，并为客户提供个性化服务，如刻字定制。NovaCustom的笔记本电脑起价1,770欧元，提供高度隐私保护和定制选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NovaCustom与其他笔记本厂商（如Framework）的比较，以及对NovaCustom产品特点的评价和争议。

不同观点：
• cosmic_cheese认为NovaCustom类似于System76或Tuxedo，因为它们可能使用的是Clevo/Tongfang等厂商的重新贴牌硬件，而非像Framework那样自行设计硬件。这种模式使得NovaCustom与Framework有所区别。

• necovek指出NovaCustom的主要卖点是开源的coreboot固件和禁用Intel ME（Intel管理引擎），但仅凭这些功能并不能使NovaCustom成为Framework的替代品。

• princevegeta89对NovaCustom提出的隐私问题表示困惑，认为Framework的硬件透明且可替换，软件选择自由，已经具有很高的透明度，质疑所谓的隐私问题是否真实存在。

• mgerdts对NovaCustom的高端定价与所配备的NVMe驱动器（使用主机内存缓冲HMB技术）表示不满，指出像WD SN850x这样性能更好的驱动器在亚马逊上的价格比NovaCustom标配的GOODRAM驱动器更低。

• speedgoose认为NovaCustom的8GB vRAM在2025年会显得非常有限，无法运行较大的语言模型，从而限制了其在某些高性能计算任务中的应用。

• getcrunk对NovaCustom的现代硬件和支持coreboot及Tails系统表示赞赏，但认为该公司缺乏像Framework那样的良好声誉和信任度。

• horsellama则对NovaCustom允许自定义超级键和配备Nvidia GPU表示欢迎，认为这可能是一款理想的笔记本。

补充讨论：
• NovaCustom的开放源代码固件和禁用Intel ME功能是吸引部分用户的关键特点，但这些特点是否足以使其成为Framework的有力竞争者存在争议。
• 部分用户对NovaCustom的定价与硬件配置之间的匹配度提出质疑，特别是与市场上其他同类产品的对比。
• 用户对NovaCustom的硬件性能（如vRAM限制）及其公司声誉和市场信任度存在不同程度的担忧和期待。

本文讨论了评估长文本问答系统时面临的挑战和关键指标。随着文档长度增加，如技术文档、小说或多文档场景，信息过载、位置差异、多跳推理和模型幻觉等问题变得更加突出。评估问答系统不仅要考虑答案的准确性，还要关注**忠实性**和**有用性**两个维度：

1. **忠实性**：答案是否严格基于源文档，不添加外部信息或捏造内容。特别在法律、金融等领域，答案必须基于给定文本。系统还需知道何时应回答“不知道”。
   
2. **有用性**：答案是否相关、详细且简洁。它应直接回应问题，包含必要细节，且简洁明了。

此外，引文准确性也是评估标准之一，确保引用的文本支持答案。文章还提到如何构建评估数据集及使用人类标注和LLM评估问答性能，并回顾了多个基准测试。

Evaluating Long-Context Question & Answer Systems
[
llm
eval
survey
]
· 28 min read
While evaluating Q&A systems is straightforward with short paragraphs, complexity increases as documents grow larger. For example, technical documentation, novels and movies, as well as multi-document scenarios. Although some of these evaluation challenges also appear in shorter contexts, long-context evaluation amplifies issues such as:
Information overload:
Irrelevant details in large documents obscure relevant facts, making it harder for retrievers and models to locate the right evidence for the answer.
Positional variance:
Evidence may appear at the beginning, middle, or end of documents, making it a challenge for models with limited effective context or those susceptible to the “lost in the middle” problem.
Multi-hop reasoning:
The correct answer depends on synthesizing several distinct pieces of evidence scattered throughout the text(s), challenging the model’s ability to retain and integrate information that is far apart.
Hallucinations at scale:
Larger contexts increase the risk of models returning plausible yet incorrect responses due to poor retrieval or limited effective context.
Open-ended questions:
Queries on broad themes or interpretative topics rarely have a single definitive answer, especially for large documents or corpora.
In this write-up, we’ll explore
key evaluation metrics
, how to
build evaluation datasets
, and
methods to assess Q&A performance
through human annotations and LLM-evaluators. We’ll also
review several benchmarks
across narrative stories, technical and academic texts, and very long-context, multi-document situations. Finally, we’ll wrap up with advice for evaluating long-context Q&A on our specific use cases.
An overview of what we'll cover in this writeup
By the way, if you want to learn more about evals, my friends Hamel and Shreya are hosting their
final
cohort of “AI Evals for Engineers and PMs” in July. Here’s a
35% discount code
.
Key Evaluation Metrics
Evaluating Q&A systems goes beyond just checking for factual accuracy. Specifically, we might want answers to be based solely on the provided text, not the model’s knowledge. But even technically correct answers aren’t necessarily helpful. Thus, to evaluate Q&A systems effectively, we should consider two orthogonal dimensions:
Faithfulness:
How strictly the answer relies on only the source document.
Helpfulness:
How relevant, comprehensive, and useful the response is for the user.
Faithfulness measures whether an answer strictly relies
only
on the source document.
This means the model shouldn’t add external information or make things up (aka hallucinate). Faithfulness is especially important for legal agreements, financial contracts, or medical and insurance forms, where answers must be based solely on the given text. Faithfulness is synonymous with groundedness, where answers must be anchored on the original document.
Faithfulness also includes the Q&A system knowing when to say, “I don’t know.” If the source document doesn’t contain the answer, the ideal response is something like, “I don’t have that information in the provided text.” Related to this challenge are two errors by Q&A systems:
False positives:
When the system makes up an answer that doesn’t exist in the source document (hallucinations).
False negatives:
When the system incorrectly states that the source document doesn’t contain information that actually is present, either due to poor retrieval or attention limitations over large contexts.
We also want to distinguish faithfulness from correctness. An answer might be correct based on general knowledge but still be unfaithful if it contradicts the document. Examples include patient-specific medical instructions that differ from the usual guidelines, definitions in financial or legal agreements that depart from the standard, and historical fiction with alternate timelines. Users depend on Q&A systems to return responses that are faithful to their specific documents, rather than general truths.
For systems that provide citations, we can also assess citation accuracy. This evaluates if the cited text supports the answer. Benchmarks like
QASPER
explicitly evaluate whether models reference the right supporting evidence for the answer. This combined assessment—checking both faithfulness and citation accuracy—provides finer-grained metrics on overall faithfulness and evidence retrieval.
However, a faithful answer isn’t always a helpful answer.
This is where we also want to evaluate the helpfulness of responses.
Helpfulness measures whether an answer is relevant, sufficiently detailed, yet concise.
Relevance means the answer directly addresses the user’s question without straying off-topic. Comprehensiveness ensures the answer contains the necessary details. Conciseness balances comprehensiveness by ensuring the answer is succinct, without unnecessary details or fluff.

data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了互联网中两种主要的电子邮件格式：纯文本和HTML，并强调了技术社区更偏好使用纯文本邮件。文章提供了如何在不同邮件客户端中设置纯文本邮件的指南，推荐了如aerc、alpine、Claws Mail等支持纯文本的客户端，并详细说明了在Apple Mail、Gmail、Thunderbird等流行客户端中设置纯文本的方法。此外，文章还介绍了纯文本邮件的礼仪建议，如引用文本和底部发帖的规范，并解释了为什么纯文本优于HTML。文章最后由sourcehut平台赞助，该平台使用纯文本邮件进行软件开发协作。

不同观点：
• **支持plain text邮件**：
  - **rsync**：认为plain text邮件美观、轻量、高效，且能避免网络追踪和隐私泄露。
  - **beached_whale**：建议关闭自动下载图片功能，以防止追踪。

• **对plain text邮件的批评**：
  - **F3nd0**：plain text邮件的引用格式处理麻烦，多层引用会导致格式混乱。

  - **kelnos**：认为许多反对HTML邮件的理由不成立，HTML本身具有无障碍功能，且发送HTML邮件并不意味着要进行钓鱼或隐私侵犯。

• **技术细节与工具**：

- **争议焦点**：plain text与HTML邮件格式的优劣之争，特别是关于可访问性、格式处理和隐私保护的讨论。

- **用户体验**：不同格式和设置对收件人体验的影响，以及如何根据收件人的需求和客户端选择合适的邮件格式。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对信息安全和政府及犯罪组织能力的关注

不同观点：
• [RRWagner] 认为，政府的强大数据收集能力最终会导致这些信息落入针对普通人的犯罪分子手中，强调信息泄露的潜在风险。该评论暗示了政府和犯罪组织都可能滥用个人数据。

• [firefax] 关注个人在日常生活中对信息安全的忽视，特别是对手机未在非使用状态下切换至飞行模式的做法表示惊讶。这表明个人信息保护意识不足是另一个值得关注的问题。

• [richardatlarge] 则将焦点放在执法机构（FBI）低估犯罪组织（如卡特尔）能力的风险上，认为执法机构应该对犯罪组织的能力有更清醒的认识，以更好地应对威胁。

补充讨论：
- [RRWagner] 和 [firefax] 的评论都涉及信息安全问题，但前者侧重于宏观层面的政府数据收集和犯罪分子获取信息的潜在关联，而后者则关注个人在日常行为中对信息安全的忽视。
- [richardatlarge] 的评论更侧重于执法机构对有组织犯罪的低估，这涉及到政府机构在对抗犯罪组织时可能存在的策略和判断失误问题。
- 争议的焦点可能在于信息安全的责任归属：是政府在信息收集和保护方面的责任，还是个人对自我信息保护的责任，亦或是执法机构在打击犯罪组织时的能力评估问题。

data.title: Why the moon shimmers with shiny glass beads
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了月球表面发现的微小玻璃珠的形成原因及其科学价值。这些玻璃珠形成于约33至36亿年前月球的火山喷发，当时月球仍年轻。每个珠体如同月球内部的微小时间胶囊，保存了古代月球火山活动的记录。研究团队利用现代显微分析技术，如纳米二次离子质谱仪和扫描电子显微镜，对这些珠体进行了详细分析。研究发现，这些玻璃珠不仅颜色和形状独特，其化学成分也与地球上的物质不同，揭示了月球火山喷发风格随时间的变化。该研究发表在《Icarus》期刊上，为理解月球早期地质活动提供了重要线索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：阿波罗宇航员发现的微小橙色珠状物揭示了月球的爆炸性过去，以及其对月球经济和未来探索的影响。

不同观点：
• 观点一：一些评论者对这一发现的历史价值表示兴奋，认为这些珠状物为研究月球火山活动和地质历史提供了重要线索。他们强调这些发现有助于理解月球的演化过程。

• 观点二：另一部分评论者则更关注这些珠状物的实际应用价值，特别是它们在未来月球资源开发中的潜力。他们讨论了这些物质是否可以用于制造陶瓷材料，从而支持月球上的长期居住和工业发展。

• 观点三：有评论者持怀疑态度，认为当前对珠状物的分析仍不够充分，需要更多实验和数据来验证其成分和形成机制。他们指出，科学界应谨慎对待这些初步发现，避免过度解读。

• 观点四：还有评论者将讨论引向更广泛的太空探索和经济前景，探讨这些发现如何影响国际空间竞赛和各国在月球资源利用上的策略。

补充讨论：
• 一个争议焦点在于这些珠状物的具体形成机制及其在科学研究中的定位。部分评论者认为，虽然这些珠状物提供了月球爆炸性过去的证据，但其科学价值仍需进一步研究确认。

• 有评论提到当前技术能力和科研资源的局限性，认为在月球上进行更深入的实地研究需要国际合作和大量投资。

• 一些评论还涉及到珠状物发现对公众理解太空探索的重要性，强调这类发现能够激发公众对科学和太空探索的兴趣，从而推动相关教育和科普活动。

The GIST
Why the moon shimmers with shiny glass beads
by Chris Woolston,
Washington University in St. Louis
edited by
Robert Egan
Editors' notes

editorial process
and
policies

Schematic diagram of a lunar lava fountaining volcanic eruption. Two glass bead trajectories through the volcanic gas cloud are illustrated with the arrowed lines (one lofted, one shallow). Three stages of bead evolution are depicted: 1) outgassing, 2) ingassing, 3) desublimation/condensation. Credit:
Icarus
(2025). DOI: 10.1016/j.icarus.2025.116607
The Apollo astronauts didn't know what they'd find when they explored the surface of the moon, but they certainly didn't expect to see drifts of tiny, bright orange glass beads glistening among the otherwise monochrome piles of rocks and dust.
The
beads
, each less than 1 mm across, formed some 3.3 to 3.6 billion years ago during
volcanic eruptions
on the surface of the then-young satellite. "They're some of the most amazing extraterrestrial samples we have," said Ryan Ogliore, an associate professor of physics in Arts & Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis, home to a large repository of lunar samples that were returned to Earth. "The beads are tiny, pristine capsules of the lunar interior."
Using a variety of microscopic analysis techniques not available when the Apollo astronauts first returned samples from the moon, Ogliore and a team of researchers have been able to take a close look at the microscopic mineral deposits on the outside of lunar beads. The unprecedented view of the ancient lunar artifacts was published in
Icarus
. The investigation was led by Thomas Williams, Stephen Parman and Alberto Saal from Brown University.
The study relied, in part, on the NanoSIMS 50, an instrument at WashU that uses a high-energy ion beam to break apart small samples of material for analysis. WashU researchers have used the device for decades to study interplanetary dust particles, presolar grains in meteorites, and other small bits of debris from our solar system.
SEM images of features on the surface of 74001 black glass beads. Credit:
Icarus
(2025). DOI: 10.1016/j.icarus.2025.116607
The study combined a variety of techniques—atom probe tomography, scanning electron microscopy, transmission
electron microscopy
and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy—at other institutions to get a closer look at the surface of the beads. "We've had these samples for 50 years, but we now have the technology to fully understand them," Ogliore said. "Many of these instruments would have been unimaginable when the beads were first collected."
As Ogliore explained, each glass bead tells its own story of the moon's past. The beads—some shiny orange, some glossy black—formed when lunar volcanoes shot material from the interior to the surface, where each drop of lava solidified instantly in the cold vacuum that surrounds the moon.
"The very existence of these beads tells us the moon had explosive eruptions, something like the fire fountains you can see in Hawaii today," he said. Because of their origins, the beads have a color, shape and
chemical composition
unlike anything found on Earth.
Tiny minerals on the surface of the beads could react with oxygen and other components of Earth's atmosphere. To avoid this possibility, the researchers extracted beads from deep within samples and kept them protected from air exposure through every step of the analysis. "Even with the advanced techniques we used, these were very difficult measurements to make," Ogliore said.
The minerals (including zinc sulfides) and isotopic composition of the bead surfaces serve as probes into the different pressure, temperature and chemical environment of lunar eruptions 3.5 billion years ago. Analyses of orange and black lunar beads have shown that the style of volcanic eruptions changed over time. "It's like reading the journal of an ancient lunar volcanologist," Ogliore said.
More information:
T.A. Williams et al, Lunar volcanic gas cloud chemistry: Constraints from glass bead surface sublimates,
Icarus
(2025).

data.title: H1-B visas hurt one type of worker and exploit another
data.author: 1vuio0pswjnm7
data.article_summary: 本文由参议员伯尼·桑德斯撰写，批评H-1B签证计划伤害美国工人并剥削外籍劳工。文章指出，该计划本应用于解决高技能人才短缺，但实际上被大公司用来雇佣廉价外籍劳工，取代美国员工，导致美国技术人员失业。同时，外籍劳工面临不公平工作条件，签证受制于雇主。桑德斯呼吁，应大幅提高签证费用，确保该计划仅作为短期解决方案，长期应通过教育提升美国竞争力，而非依赖廉价外籍劳工。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何改革美国的客工签证项目（如H1-B）以及相关费用，以更好地服务美国工人并吸引全球人才。

不同观点：
• [sxp的观点]  
  - 支持大幅提高大公司支付的客工费用，以资助美国工人的奖学金、学徒项目和工作培训机会。  
  - 建议将H1-B项目改为拍卖机制，取消配额和抽签制度，让企业通过竞拍获得名额，并可以从联邦所得税中扣除费用。  
  - 认为企业若想获得全球最优秀的人才，应愿意为此支付高额费用。

• [digianarchist的观点]  
  - 部分同意[sxp]的观点，但指出目前已有针对顶尖人才的签证类别（O1签证），H1-B并非唯一选择。  
  - 认为H1-B是目前通过就业移民美国的合理途径，尤其对于那些没有移民经验的雇主和员工而言。  
  - 指出EB2/3移民签证程序复杂，雇主通常不愿意为不熟悉的员工办理此类签证，因为员工可以在入境后为其他公司工作。

• [downrightmike的观点]  
  - 认为外包（outsourcing）问题比签证问题严重得多（1,000% worse），暗示应更关注外包对美国就业市场的负面影响。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一是如何在吸引全球优秀人才和保护美国工人利益之间取得平衡。  
- 另一个讨论点是不同签证类别（H1-B vs. O1 vs. EB2/3）的适用性和实际操作中的困难。  
- [downrightmike]的评论引入了外包问题，尽管未详细展开，但显示出对外包现象的强烈反对。

44407121.article_content:
H1-B visas hurt one type of worker and exploit another. This mess must be fixed
January 8, 2025
By: Sen. Bernie Sanders;
Fox News
It must never be cheaper for a corporation to hire a guest worker from overseas than an American worker
We are living in a moment with unprecedented income and wealth inequality.  At a time when the richest people in our country have never had it so good, 60% of Americans are living paycheck to paycheck and inflation-adjusted income for the average American worker has been stagnant for 50 years. Why is that?
How did it happen that the three richest men in America own more wealth than the bottom half of our society while so many of our people struggle to afford the high cost of rent, groceries and other basic necessities of life?
It’s time to take a hard look at some of the economic policies which have made the rich much richer while many Americans continue to fall further and further behind.
Thirty years ago, the leaders of corporate America, the political establishment in both major parties and the editorial boards of influential newspapers told us not to worry about the loss of blue-collar manufacturing jobs that would come as a result of unfettered free trade agreements like NAFTA and Permanent Normal Trade Relations with China (PNTR). They promised that those lost jobs would be more than offset by the many good-paying, white-collar information technology jobs that would be created in the United States.  I never believed that and voted against those agreements.
Unfortunately, I, and the many others who opposed those trade deals, were proven correct. NAFTA and PNTR cost us millions of good-paying manufacturing jobs as large corporations shut down thousands of factories in America and fled to China, Mexico, and other low-wage countries in search of cheap labor.
And what about all of the great high-tech jobs that would be created?  Well, that didn’t quite happen either.  As a result of the H-1B guest worker program, major corporations are now importing hundreds of thousands of low-paid guest workers from abroad to fill the white-collar technology jobs that are available.  In other words, “Heads billionaires win. Tails American workers lose.”
In recent weeks, the H-1B program has sparked intense debate. Billionaires like Elon Musk claim it is crucial to our economy, arguing that the United States faces a shortage of highly skilled engineers and technology professionals. They are dead wrong.
The primary purpose of H-1B and other guest worker programs is not to employ the “best and the brightest,” but instead to replace American workers with lower-paid workers from abroad who often live as indentured servants.  The cheaper it is to hire guest workers, the more money the multi-billionaire owners of large corporations make.
Not only is this program disastrous for American workers, it can be very harmful to guest workers as well, who are often locked into lower-paying jobs and can have their visas taken away from them by their corporate bosses if they complain about dangerous, unfair or illegal working conditions.
Between 2022 and 2023, the top companies using the H-1B program laid off 85,000 American workers, while simultaneously bringing in over 34,000 guest workers from abroad. Meanwhile, millions of Americans with advanced degrees in STEM fields are unable to find work in their areas of expertise.
If there is truly a major shortage of skilled tech workers in this country, why did Tesla lay-off over 7,500 American workers last year – including many software developers and engineers at its factory in Austin, Texas – while applying to hire thousands of H-1B guest workers?
If these jobs are only going to “the best and brightest,” why has Tesla employed H-1B guest workers as associate accountants for as little as $58,000, associate mechanical engineers for as little as $70,000 a year, and associate material planners for as little as $80,000 a year? Those don’t sound like highly specialized jobs that are for the top 0.1 percent, as Musk claimed last month. Musk has failed to address concerns about Tesla’s use of H-1B visas for its employees.
If this program is really supposed to be about importing workers with highly advanced degrees in science and technology, why are H-1B guest workers being employed as lawyers, dog trainers, massage therapists, cooks, and English teachers? Can we really not find English teachers in America?  Do we really believe that we are facing a dire shortage of lawyers in our country?
Let’s be clear. To the extent that there may be labor shortages in our country in some highly specialized areas that need to be filled by employees from abroad through the H-1B program, we need to make sure that this program is used as a short-term fix.
Long-term, if the United States is going to succeed in a highly competitive global economy, we must have the best-educated workforce in the world.
And one way to help make that happen is to substantially increase the guest worker fees

  - 指出EB2/3移民签证程序复杂，雇主通常不愿意为不熟悉的员工办理此类签证，因为员工可以在入境后为其他公司工作。

• [downrightmike的观点]  
  - 认为外包（outsourcing）问题比签证问题严重得多（1,000% worse），暗示应更关注外包对美国就业市场的负面影响。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一是如何在吸引全球优秀人才和保护美国工人利益之间取得平衡。  
- 另一个讨论点是不同签证类别（H1-B vs. O1 vs. EB2/3）的适用性和实际操作中的困难。  
- [downrightmike]的评论引入了外包问题，尽管未详细展开，但显示出对外包现象的强烈反对。

主要讨论点：Meta公司在AI领域的战略、组织文化、投资决策以及在AI竞赛中的地位。

不同观点：
• **KaiserPro**：认为Meta的AI部门存在严重的文化和组织问题。GenAI团队扩张过快，导致效率低下；FAIR团队因内部管理和人事问题失去活力；RL-R团队虽有潜力，但受限于不切实际的项目目标和内部管理问题。KaiserPro特别批评了领导层缺乏应用ML的经验以及在产品化上的困难。

• **andrewparker**：关注Meta在Scale投资上的策略，认为Meta选择49%的投资而非完全收购是为了避免全球监管审查。这种做法不仅对Meta有利，也为Scale的股东提供了继续发展业务的机会，是一种双赢的策略。

• **vagabund**：对KaiserPro的一些观点提出异议，特别是关于数据标注和LLM模型训练的复杂性。vagabund指出，数据标注在RL中的作用不仅仅是机械性的工作，而是具有高度策略性的价值。此外，训练大规模竞争性模型并非易事，涉及许多技术诀窍和商业秘密。

• **duxup**：对AI模型的基准测试和实际用户体验之间的差距提出疑问，指出尽管模型在基准测试中表现良好，但实际使用中并未显著改善，反映了用户体验与技术指标之间的脱节。

• **blobbers**：以讽刺的语气评论Meta在数据标注上的巨额花费，质疑其投资效益和实际成果。

• **paulpauper**：指出Meta尽管在亏损项目上花费巨资，但因其广告网络的盈利能力，股票仍然表现良好，反映了市场对Meta的信心。

• **DataDaemon**：提到Meta在元宇宙项目上的巨额花费，并将其与当前在AI项目上的投资进行对比，质疑Meta的资金使用效率和投资策略。

• **nothrowaways**：质疑Meta在AI竞赛中落后的观点，要求提供更多证据和解释。

• **dangus**：批评Meta的管理层和CEO扎克伯格的领导能力，认为Meta在产品创新上依赖收购，且因信任问题在推出新产品时受到限制。此外，指出Meta花费巨资希望通过外部公司获得新的成功，反映其自身创新能力的不足。

补充讨论：
• Meta在AI领域的投资和项目管理问题，特别是组织文化和领导决策对项目成功的影响。
• 对AI技术发展的实际进展和市场应用的质疑，特别是基准测试与用户体验之间的差距。
• Meta在面对监管和市场竞争时的策略选择，以及这些选择对其长期发展的影响。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软针对初创企业的Azure信用额度调整及其竞争对手（AWS、Google）的对比

不同观点：
• **[js4ever]** 认为虽然微软可能因为防止滥用而调整了信用额度计划，但Azure的信用额度仍然是避免过度开支的一个良好信号。他还指出，通过其他服务提供商（如Hetzner）可以用更少的资金获得等同于150K Azure信用额度的资源，暗示微软的新方案可能不再那么有竞争力。

• **[zadams]** 提供了微软调整信用额度计划的具体细节。新的计划将根据初创企业是否有投资者关联分为两个等级：有投资者关联的初创企业可以获得10万美元的Azure信用额度，而没有投资者关联的企业只能获得5千美元的额度。这一变化与此前的四级信用额度体系有明显差异，特别是未获得投资的初创企业获得的额度大幅减少。

• **[malux85]** 分享了自己使用微软Azure服务的负面体验，并与AWS和Google的服务进行了对比。他指出微软的GPU资源不可用，技术基础设施受限，服务响应慢，且账单系统混乱（如错误扣费和难以追回款项）。他还提到与AWS和Google的良好体验，如被邀请参加社交活动、获得客户支持以及得到更多的技术资源。总体上，他认为微软Azure的服务质量远不如AWS和Google。

补充讨论：
• 微软对初创企业的支持政策发生了显著变化，特别是未获投资的企业获得的Azure信用额度大幅减少，这可能引发一些初创企业的不满。
• 不同用户对微软Azure服务的体验差异较大，**[malux85]** 的批评集中在技术支持、资源可用性和账单系统的混乱上，而**[js4ever]** 则关注了价格和信用额度的性价比问题。
• AWS和Google的服务被**[malux85]** 作为正面例子提出，表明它们在客户支持、资源获取和技术服务方面优于微软Azure，这可能反映了微软在某些方面的竞争劣势。

争议焦点：
• 微软对Azure信用额度政策的调整是否合理，尤其是对未获投资企业的额度削减是否会影响初创企业的选择。
• 用户**[malux85]** 的负面体验是否具有普遍性，其他用户是否也面临类似的技术支持和服务问题。

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了为何历任美国总统都难以让美国摆脱对中东战争的介入。尽管每位总统都表示希望让美国从该地区冲突中抽身，但最终都进行了军事干预，如里根时期的利比亚空袭、老布什的海湾战争、克林顿对伊拉克和阿尔盖达的空袭、小布什的伊拉克入侵、奥巴马的多国反恐行动、特朗普对伊朗军事领导人的刺杀等。即使特朗普曾批评中东干预政策，并试图将战略重心转向中国，但当前危机又使其加大了对中东的军事投入。中东持续的危机和其在全球能源、安全格局中的重要性，使得美国难以真正从中东撤出。文章将此现象比喻为“迈克尔·科里昂时刻”，即每次想脱身却被拉回。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于网络存档服务（如archive.today）的使用及其道德与法律问题

不同观点：

• **支持使用网络存档服务**  
  支持者认为，网络存档服务在保存重要信息和防止链接失效（链接腐烂）方面具有重要价值。例如，用户[whstl]提到，这些服务有助于保存那些可能被修改或删除的网页内容，确保信息的长期可访问性。特别是在处理可能存在偏见或选择性修改的媒体报道时，网络存档被视为一种可靠的验证工具。支持者还指出，存档服务能帮助研究人员、记者和普通用户追踪信息变化，具有学术和新闻价值。

• **反对及担忧道德与法律问题**  
  反对者或持怀疑态度的人则主要关注存档服务的道德和法律风险。他们指出，未经网站所有者同意而复制网页内容可能涉及侵犯版权。此外，某些网站可能明确禁止存档其内容，而存档服务却无视这些规定，可能引发法律纠纷。一些评论者还担心，存档服务可能被滥用，用于传播未经核实的信息或侵犯隐私。例如，某些用户可能利用存档服务访问那些因法律原因被删除或修正的内容，从而绕过正常的监管机制。

• **存档服务的操作透明性与责任问题**  
  有评论提到，存档服务在透明性和责任承担方面存在不足。一些用户质疑存档服务是否应公开其存档标准和删除政策，尤其是在涉及敏感内容或错误存档时。例如，如果某个网站所有者要求删除其被存档的内容，存档服务应如何响应？有评论认为，这类服务应设立更加明确的操作规范和投诉机制，以平衡信息保存和内容所有者的权益。

补充讨论：

• **存档服务的可靠性与技术局限**  
  部分讨论集中于存档服务的可靠性和技术局限。例如，有用户指出，某些网页内容可能无法被完整保存，特别是涉及动态内容、交互功能或受保护的媒体文件时。此外，存档服务的服务器宕机或关闭也可能导致存档内容暂时或永久不可访问，削弱其保存信息的价值。

• **争议焦点：公共利益与个人权利的平衡**  
  整个讨论的核心争议在于如何平衡公共利益与个人权利。支持者强调存档服务对公众知情权和信息保存的重要性，而反对者则更关注版权、隐私和网站所有者的控制权。这一矛盾在涉及政治、新闻和学术领域的敏感内容时尤为突出。

总结：讨论主要围绕网络存档服务的价值与风险展开，涉及信息保存的必要性、法律和道德问题、操作透明性及技术局限等方面。争议的焦点是如何在公共利益与个人权利之间找到合适的平衡点。

Why the US just can’t quit Middle East wars
Every president wants to extricate America from the region’s conflicts. None of them do.
by
Joshua Keating
Jun 25, 2025, 5:30 PM UTC
Facebook
Link
A view of the famous anti-US mural in central Tehran, Iran, that depicts the US flag with bombs and skulls on April 10.
Hossein Beris/Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images
Joshua Keating
is a senior correspondent at Vox covering foreign policy and world news with a focus on the future of international conflict. He is the author of the 2018 book,
Invisible Countries: Journeys to the Edge of Nationhood
, an exploration of border conflicts, unrecognized countries, and changes to the world map.
In April 1980, President Jimmy Carter authorized Operation Eagle Claw, an
ill-fated military operation
to rescue the American hostages held at the US embassy in Iran. Since then, every US president has ordered at least one — usually more than one — military intervention in the Middle East and North Africa.
Under Ronald Reagan, there was the
bombing of Libya
and the
deployment of Marines to Lebanon
. Under George H.W. Bush, there was Operation Desert Storm. Under Bill Clinton, airstrikes against
Saddam Hussein’s regime in Iraq
and against
al-Qaeda in Sudan
. Under George W. Bush, the invasion of Iraq. Under Barack Obama, a multicountry counterterrorist drone campaign, the toppling of Muammar al-Qaddafi’s regime in Libya, and the redeployment of US troops to Iraq to fight ISIS. Under Donald Trump’s first term, an expanded campaign against ISIS, missile strikes against the Syrian regime, and the targeted assassination of
Iran’s most powerful military leaders
. Under Joe Biden, the deployment of US troops to the region following the October 7, 2023, attack and the airstrikes against Yemen’s Houthi rebels.
Now, in his second term, Trump has crossed another Rubicon, becoming the first US president to
use military force
on the soil of America’s longtime adversary, Iran. Though a ceasefire has now been declared, it’s very possible this crisis is only beginning, particularly if, as US
intelligence agencies reportedly believe
, much of Iran’s nuclear program is still intact after the strikes.
Trump’s pivot toward the Middle East is a surprising turn from this president. This is a very different message from the one he delivered in Saudi Arabia just last month
when he decried
“neocons” and “interventionists” for ill-considered attempts to remake the region through force. Trump has
said in the past
, in reference to the Iraq war, that “GOING INTO THE MIDDLE EAST IS THE WORST DECISION EVER MADE IN THE HISTORY OF OUR COUNTRY,” and he has generally appeared to view the region — apart from wealthy Gulf States — as a
hopeless war zone
with little to offer the US.
While he was often stymied in his attempts to withdraw troops in his first term by hawkish advisers, this time
many of his senior appointees
have been so-called “restrainers,” who advocate pulling back from US military commitments overseas or “prioritizers,” who want to shift attention to what they see as the more important challenge posed by China. Until very recently, they appeared to have the upper hand. But in the current crisis, the US actually
relocated important military assets
from
the Pacific to the Middle East to the
consternation of some Pentagon officials
.
The stated desire to end “endless wars” in the Middle East and shift to bigger priorities is something the Trump administration has in common with the other two post-Iraq war presidencies. Barack Obama was elected in large part because of his opposition to the war in Iraq. In 2011, his secretary of state, Hillary Clinton,
promised a “pivot”
to Asia and the Pacific for US foreign policy priorities. The Arab Spring and the rise of ISIS got in the way of that, and the phrase “pivot to Asia” became a running joke in US foreign policy circles. Joe Biden withdrew US troops from Afghanistan — not a Middle Eastern country but very much the archetypal “endless war” of the post-9/11 era — and put forward a foreign policy vision emphasizing
great power competition with China
. His national security adviser infamously described the Middle East as “quieter than it has been in decades” just days before the October 7 attacks shattered that quiet and shifted his boss’s priorities.
“Right now, President Trump is having what I call his ‘Michael Corleone’ moment, and at some point, every president has one,” said Brian Katulis, a senior fellow at the Middle East Institute, referring to
Al Pacino’s famous line
in
The Godfather III
, “Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in.”
But why does this dynamic keep repeating? Why, 45 years after Operation Eagle Claw and 22 after the invasion of Iraq, can’t the US military “get out” of this region?
The Middle East is still important…and still has a lot of problems
One big reason why the US keeps getting drawn into the Middle East’s crises is that those crises keep happ

主要讨论点：关于网络存档服务（如archive.today）的使用及其道德与法律问题

不同观点：

• **支持使用网络存档服务**  
  支持者认为，网络存档服务在保存重要信息和防止链接失效（链接腐烂）方面具有重要价值。例如，用户[whstl]提到，这些服务有助于保存那些可能被修改或删除的网页内容，确保信息的长期可访问性。特别是在处理可能存在偏见或选择性修改的媒体报道时，网络存档被视为一种可靠的验证工具。支持者还指出，存档服务能帮助研究人员、记者和普通用户追踪信息变化，具有学术和新闻价值。

• **反对及担忧道德与法律问题**  
  反对者或持怀疑态度的人则主要关注存档服务的道德和法律风险。他们指出，未经网站所有者同意而复制网页内容可能涉及侵犯版权。此外，某些网站可能明确禁止存档其内容，而存档服务却无视这些规定，可能引发法律纠纷。一些评论者还担心，存档服务可能被滥用，用于传播未经核实的信息或侵犯隐私。例如，某些用户可能利用存档服务访问那些因法律原因被删除或修正的内容，从而绕过正常的监管机制。

• **存档服务的操作透明性与责任问题**  
  有评论提到，存档服务在透明性和责任承担方面存在不足。一些用户质疑存档服务是否应公开其存档标准和删除政策，尤其是在涉及敏感内容或错误存档时。例如，如果某个网站所有者要求删除其被存档的内容，存档服务应如何响应？有评论认为，这类服务应设立更加明确的操作规范和投诉机制，以平衡信息保存和内容所有者的权益。

补充讨论：

• **存档服务的可靠性与技术局限**  
  部分讨论集中于存档服务的可靠性和技术局限。例如，有用户指出，某些网页内容可能无法被完整保存，特别是涉及动态内容、交互功能或受保护的媒体文件时。此外，存档服务的服务器宕机或关闭也可能导致存档内容暂时或永久不可访问，削弱其保存信息的价值。

• **争议焦点：公共利益与个人权利的平衡**  
  整个讨论的核心争议在于如何平衡公共利益与个人权利。支持者强调存档服务对公众知情权和信息保存的重要性，而反对者则更关注版权、隐私和网站所有者的控制权。这一矛盾在涉及政治、新闻和学术领域的敏感内容时尤为突出。

总结：讨论主要围绕网络存档服务的价值与风险展开，涉及信息保存的必要性、法律和道德问题、操作透明性及技术局限等方面。争议的焦点是如何在公共利益与个人权利之间找到合适的平衡点。

data.author: lnyan
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了新一代多模态模型Qwen VLo，它不仅能“理解”图像内容，还能基于该理解生成高质量的图像，实现从感知到创作的跨越。该模型通过渐进生成方法，从左到右、从上到下构建图像，并不断优化预测，确保结果的连贯性和和谐性。Qwen VLo在内容理解和生成方面更加精准，能保持语义一致性，支持基于开放指令的编辑，如风格转换、背景更换、物体修改等，并能处理检测和分割任务。此外，它支持中英多语言指令，方便全球用户使用。文章还展示了多个示例，如根据用户指令生成柴犬图像并进行各种修改和风格转换。用户可通过Qwen Chat访问该模型。

QWEN CHAT
DISCORD
Introduction
#
The evolution of multimodal large models is continually pushing the boundaries of what we believe technology can achieve. From the initial QwenVL to the latest Qwen2.5 VL, we have made progress in enhancing the model’s ability to understand image content. Today, we are excited to introduce a new model, Qwen VLo, a unified multimodal understanding and generation model. This newly upgraded model not only “understands” the world but also generates high-quality recreations based on that understanding, truly bridging the gap between perception and creation. Note that this is a preview version and you can access it through Qwen Chat. You can directly send a prompt like “Generate a picture of a cute cat” to generate an image or upload an image of a cat and ask “Add a cap on the cat’s head” to modify an image. The image generation process is shown below.
The Creative Process: Turn Your Imagination Into Reality
As demonstrated in the video showcasing the generative process, Qwen VLo employs a progressive generation method, gradually constructing the entire image from left to right and top to bottom. During this process, the model continuously refines and optimizes its predictions to ensure that the final result is coherent and harmonious. This generative mechanism not only enhances visual quality but also provides users with a more flexible and controllable creative experience.
From Understanding to Creation: Enhanced Multimodal Generation Capabilities
#
Qwen VLo has undergone a comprehensive upgrade in both its original multimodal understanding and generation capabilities. It significantly deepens its comprehension of image content and achieves more accurate and consistent generation results. Below are the core highlights of Qwen VLo:
More Precise Content Understanding and Recreation
Previous multimodal models often struggled with semantic inconsistencies during the generation process, such as misinterpreting a car as another object or failing to retain key structural features of the original image. Qwen VLo, equipped with enhanced detail-capturing abilities, maintains a high level of semantic consistency throughout the generation process. For instance, when a user inputs a photo of a car and requests a “color change,” Qwen VLo can accurately identify the car model, preserve its original structure, and naturally transform its color style. The generated result meets expectations while maintaining realism.
Support for Open-Ended Instruction-Based Editing
Users can provide creative instructions in natural language, such as “change this painting to a Van Gogh style,” “make this photo look like it’s from the 19th century,” or “add a sunny sky to this image.” Qwen VLo can flexibly respond to these open-ended commands and produce results that align with user expectations. Whether it’s artistic style transfer, scene reconstruction, or detailed touch-ups, the model handles them all with ease. Even traditional visual perception tasks, such as predicting depth maps, segmentation maps, detection maps, and edge information, can be accomplished through simple editing instructions. Furthermore, Qwen VLo can also seamlessly handle more complex instructions — such as modifying objects, editing text, and changing backgrounds — all within a single command.
Multilingual Instruction Support
Qwen VLo supports multiple languages, including Chinese and English, breaking down language barriers and providing a unified, convenient interaction experience for global users. Regardless of the language you use, simply describe your needs, and the model will quickly understand and deliver the desired output.
Demo Cases
#
Qwen VLo acts like a human artist, using its understanding to turn imagination into reality. Below are some examples for reference.
Qwen VLo is capable of directly generating images and modifying them by replacing backgrounds, adding subjects, performing style transfers, and even executing extensive modifications based on open-ended instructions, as well as handling detection and segmentation tasks.

data.title: Weird Expressions in Rust
data.author: lukastyrychtr
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了Rust类型系统中的一些怪异表达式，这些表达式虽然看似奇怪但都是有效的Rust代码。文章通过具体示例解释了这些表达式的原理，包括：

1. **strange函数**：`return true`的类型是`!`（永不返回），它可以强制转换为任何类型，如`bool`。
2. **funny函数**：`return`可以强制转换为`()`类型，因此可以传递给参数为`()`的函数。
3. **what函数**：使用`Cell`类型，在`while`循环中设置其值，并通过闭包调用。
4. **zombiejesus函数**：大量使用`return`表达式，它们可以强制转换为不同类型。
5. **notsure函数**：涉及未初始化变量和赋值操作，利用了Rust的类型推断特性。
6. **canttouchthis函数**：结合`println!`和`return`，展示了Rust宏和表达式的灵活性。
7. **angrydome函数**：展示了`break`和`continue`在循环中的特殊用法。
8. **union函数**：展示了Rust中`union`关键字的特殊用法。
9. **punch_card函数**：展示了Rust中范围表达式（`..`和`..=`）的复杂组合。

这些示例展示了Rust类型系统的强大和灵活性，以及一些极端用例。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust语言中的特殊语法和表达式行为

不同观点：
• [steveklabnik] 认为 `evil_lincoln` 函数的语法在现代Rust中显得怪异，因为旧版Rust中 `log` 曾是打印输出的关键字，而现代Rust使用 `println!` 宏代替，导致原有的玩笑失效。同时提到该函数测试了将 `log` 的返回值保存在变量中的行为，这在实际代码中不会使用，因此显得"怪异"。
• [b0a04gl] 认为这些怪异语法是Rust将表达式作为一等公民的结果，包括块、if语句、match表达式以及返回值的宏。这种设计让Rust的语法树比大多数人的习惯更深，因此会让人觉得奇怪，但实际上是系统设计的一部分。
• [benreesman] 提到了一个名为"Ergonomic Rust"的项目，通过C++23实现消除未定义行为、边界错误以及裸指针使用等问题，强调了通过现代C++特性来增强安全性。
• [ramon156] 指出，对于Rust开发者来说，这些语法也很奇怪，需要时间去理解。
• [lacker] 纠正了对 `bathroom_stall` 代码的解释，指出在Rust中 `i += 1` 返回 `()`，因此两个 `+=` 语句总是相等的，导致 `if` 语句总是为假。
• [matt_kantor] 分享了一段复杂且难以理解的Rust代码，展示了Rust中表达式的复杂使用。
• [xg15] 作为Rust初学者，认为 `!` 类型在初始看时怪异，但理解后发现它是表示永远不会返回任何值的"伪类型"。
• [arjvik] 解释了 `return` 作为值的意义，它可以被强制转换为任何类型，以便在函数中提前返回而不产生实际值。
• [munificent] 对 `union` 不是Rust的保留字感到疑惑，因为Rust一直使用ML风格的联合类型，且 `union` 并不是特别有用的标识符。

补充讨论：
• [armchairhacker] 提到一个有关Rust的测验，展示了一些产生非直观输出或编译错误的Rust程序。

44397367.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了Rust类型系统中的一些怪异表达式，这些表达式虽然看似奇怪但都是有效的Rust代码。文章通过具体示例解释了这些表达式的原理，包括：

1. **strange函数**：`return true`的类型是`!`（永不返回），它可以强制转换为任何类型，如`bool`。
2. **funny函数**：`return`可以强制转换为`()`类型，因此可以传递给参数为`()`的函数。
3. **what函数**：使用`Cell`类型，在`while`循环中设置其值，并通过闭包调用。
4. **zombiejesus函数**：大量使用`return`表达式，它们可以强制转换为不同类型。
5. **notsure函数**：涉及未初始化变量和赋值操作，利用了Rust的类型推断特性。
6. **canttouchthis函数**：结合`println!`和`return`，展示了Rust宏和表达式的灵活性。
7. **angrydome函数**：展示了`break`和`continue`在循环中的特殊用法。
8. **union函数**：展示了Rust中`union`关键字的特殊用法。
9. **punch_card函数**：展示了Rust中范围表达式（`..`和`..=`）的复杂组合。

这些示例展示了Rust类型系统的强大和灵活性，以及一些极端用例。

data.title: Show HN: Zenta – Mindfulness for Terminal Users
data.author: ihiep
data.article_summary: **Zenta** 是一个专为终端用户设计的正念工具，帮助开发者在编码时通过呼吸保持专注。它无需跟踪或分析，仅通过简单的命令（如 `breath`、`breathe`、`reflect`）引导用户进行一次或多次呼吸练习，以重新集中注意力。Zenta 提供纯视觉的呼吸动画，支持多种终端，并自动适配不同环境。它强调正念不应被量化，真正的正念是在意识到分心时回归呼吸，而非追求数据优化。Zenta 提供预构建的二进制文件和源码编译两种安装方式，支持多个操作系统。其设计宗旨是无干扰、私密、且即时可用。

不同观点：

• **对工具的赞赏与潜在应用场景的讨论**：ofirtwo和nathell等人对Zenta的设计理念和功能表示赞赏，特别是将呼吸调节工具与工程师的工作流结合，帮助提高专注力和正念。ofirtwo还提到个人在工作时常常忽略呼吸问题，因此这种工具非常有帮助。

• **对功能扩展的建议**：nakedneuron希望增加动态调整呼吸模式的功能，尤其是通过蓝牙控制器调整呼吸节奏。slowkoder建议加入类似'focus'命令，帮助用户结合待办事项和哲理名言保持专注。five9s则建议加入自动触发呼吸提醒的功能。

• **对工具外观的反馈**：car提到在MacOS终端中运行时，显示效果与描述不符，只有一行动画。j4cobgarby提出一个小建议，希望帮助信息中能动态显示可执行文件的名称，因为手动重命名后帮助信息中的名称未更新。

• **对工具主题风格的争议**：d--b对Zenta的瑜伽和放松主题持保留态度，认为这种风格类似"spa"中的陈词滥调，更偏好摇滚风格的主题。

44394929.article_summary: **Zenta** 是一个专为终端用户设计的正念工具，帮助开发者在编码时通过呼吸保持专注。它无需跟踪或分析，仅通过简单的命令（如 `breath`、`breathe`、`reflect`）引导用户进行一次或多次呼吸练习，以重新集中注意力。Zenta 提供纯视觉的呼吸动画，支持多种终端，并自动适配不同环境。它强调正念不应被量化，真正的正念是在意识到分心时回归呼吸，而非追求数据优化。Zenta 提供预构建的二进制文件和源码编译两种安装方式，支持多个操作系统。其设计宗旨是无干扰、私密、且即时可用。

data.title: A lumberjack created more than 200 sculptures in Wisconsin's Northwoods
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary: 退休伐木工弗雷德·史密斯在20世纪40年代至60年代期间，在威斯康星州的家中创作了200多座混凝土雕塑，这些雕塑大小不一，融合了当地文化和更广泛的历史与精神象征。史密斯的作品包括从日常生活到民间英雄的各种形象，以及如萨卡加维亚和自由女神像等历史符号。他的雕塑采用木结构为核心，外包水泥，并用破碎玻璃等 found objects 装饰。如今，这些作品保存在威斯康星混凝土公园，该公园占地16英亩，位于该州北部林区。由于暴露在自然环境中，雕塑需要大量维护工作，包括使用海洋环氧树脂和硅胶密封胶等材料修复裂缝和不稳定性。公园免费开放，但鼓励捐款以支持保护工作。

44393160.article_content:
Over the years, a conservator replaced the headgear on deer with real antlers and the originals mounted on moose with synthetic alternatives.
Carol M. Highsmith/Buyenlarge/Getty Images
During Fred Smith’s golden years, art inexplicably began to pour out of him. The retired lumberjack loved to work with his hands, think with his hands, speak with his hands—and one day, like magic, he began to create with his hands.
Bent over by age and arthritis, the Phillips, Wisconsin, resident continued to build life-size and larger-than-life concrete sculptures—over 200 in all—from the late 1940s to the mid-1960s, blending local culture and lore with the wider world and the great beyond.
Smith’s homestead farm soon filled with images from his life and imagination as he depicted everything from everyday folks to folk heroes, as well as symbols of American history, patriotism and spirituality.
The sculptures are loosely organized by theme. Even so, the panorama of animals, humans and objects all seem to mix and mingle in the same landscape, leading to plenty of intriguing juxtapositions. Picture everything from Sacagawea and the Statue of Liberty to a
musky
so massive it’s pulled by a team of horses.
When asked about his monuments, Smith, who died in 1976 at 89 years old, would simply respond with laughter. “Nobody knows why I made them,”
he said
. “Not even me.”
Retired lumberjack Fred Smith built more than 200 sculptures on his farm from the late 1940s to the mid-1960s.
Wisconsin Concrete Park
Unable to read or write, he taught himself to form these sculptures using wooden structures at their core wrapped in mink or barbed wire, covered in layers of cement, and adorned with broken glass and other found objects.
Today, his eclectic display lives on at the
Wisconsin Concrete Park
, an outdoor sculpture garden situated within a
16-acre setting
in the state’s sparsely populated Northwoods region, where the trees outnumber the people.
What shines through in Smith’s work—nearly half a century after his departure—is a profound reverence for nature and for the many ordinary and extraordinary people, places and events explored throughout his art.
Preservation tools and techniques
Surviving the area’s elements, particularly the long and frigid winters, is easier said than done, though. What visitors may overlook is the painstaking upkeep that goes into these folk art statues that are exposed to Mother Nature’s whims and Father Time’s unrelenting wear and tear.
This past year, for example, a tree branch took Paul Bunyan’s head off, injured his arm and walloped one of his wolfhounds in one fell swoop, says Ann Grzywnowicz, operations manager of the
Friends of Fred Smith
, a nonprofit formed to preserve the park and develop it into an educational and cultural facility.
Restoring the legendary lumberjack to his former glory will be one of the biggest and most significant projects awaiting Ben Caguioa, a sculpture conservator based in Chicago, when he returns this summer to tackle the most recent round of destruction caused by wind, water and winter.
Need to know: How to visit the Wisconsin Concrete Park
The Wisconsin Concrete Park is located just south of Phillips, in Price County, Wisconsin.
The park is open to the public year-round during daylight hours. No admission is required, but donations are encouraged, as the funds go toward preservation work.
His toolbox includes a range of materials—such as marine epoxies, fumed silica and elastomeric caulking—meant to restore structural integrity and aesthetic appeal. This undertaking involves repairing breaks, fixing instabilities, strengthening sculptures or leveling those that have begun to tilt.
Along the way, Caguioa has replaced antlers, reinforced legs and re-leveled the big fish. He has also worked extensively on the lumberjacks near the park entrance, one of which completely collapsed and had to be rebuilt from the ground up.
Many of these sculptures were assembled around wooden two-by-fours, and these box frames—especially within the human figures—gradually decay. The armature that runs up through the legs is made of galvanized pipe that rusts out.
Since there are only two points of contact with the ground, the statues eventually begin to wobble. To reinforce ankles, Caguioa inserts stainless steel rods within the galvanized pipe or replaces that pipe with a steel rod of equivalent thickness.
On breaks and cracks, the conservator uses marine epoxies to establish a solid connection. “I’ll inject that into the cracks using a syringe,” Caguioa says. When he needs to fill a larger gap, he thickens the epoxy with fumed silica to achieve a consistency that resembles a viscous ointment. From there, Caguioa disguises the fractures using elastomeric caulking dusted with sand to replicate the appearance of the original concrete.
If the sculpture spans two or more bases or if the original base is cracked, he’ll use flexible joints to compensate for the movement, much like the
expansion join
